title.zh: 第二十八 百官五 州郡 縣鄉 亭里 匈奴中郎將 烏桓校尉 護羌校尉 王國 宋衛國 列侯 關內侯 四夷國 百官奉
title.raw: 第二十八 百官五 州郡 縣鄉 亭里 匈奴中郎將 烏桓校尉 護羌校尉 王國 宋衛國 列侯 關內侯 四夷國 百官奉 Volume 118: Officials Part Five

sentences.zh: 志第二十八 百官五

translations.literal: Treatise number twenty-eight: Officials, part five.
translations.idiomatic: Monograph 28: The fifth installment on the bureaucracy of state.

sentences.zh: 州郡 县乡 亭里 匈奴中郎将 乌桓校尉 护羌校尉 王国 宋卫国 列侯 关内侯 四夷国 百官奉

translations.literal: Provinces and commanderies; counties and townships; wards and hamlets; Herald to the Xiongnu; Protector of the Wuhuan; Protector of the Qiang; princely kingdoms; the fiefs of Song and Wei; full marquisates; marquisates-within-the-passes; states of the four quarters; salaries of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and commanderies, counties and rural townships, wards and hamlets, the Herald to the Xiongnu, the Protector of the Wuhuan, the Protector of the Qiang, princely kingdoms, the domains of Song and Wei, full marquisates and marquisates-within-the-passes, tributary states beyond the inner realm, and the stipends paid to officials.

sentences.zh: 外十二州，每州刺史一人，六百石。

translations.literal: Outside the capital there were twelve provinces; each province had one inspector, at six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the metropolitan region lay twelve provinces, each overseen by a single regional inspector at the six-hundred-picul grade.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：秦有监御史，监诸郡，汉兴省之，但遣丞相史分刺诸州，无常官。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The Qin had supervising clerks who oversaw the commanderies; when the Han arose they abolished them, and only sent out clerks from the chancellor’s office to investigate the provinces in rotation, without a permanent post.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Under the Qin, supervising clerks watched over the commanderies; the Han at first abolished the office and merely dispatched secretaries from the chancellor’s staff on rotating inspections of the provinces, with no standing appointment.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初置刺史十三人，秩六百石。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu at first established thirteen inspectors, rank six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu initially appointed thirteen regional inspectors, each at the six-hundred-picul salary level.

sentences.zh: 成帝更为牧，秩二千石。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng changed them to shepherds, rank two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng the title was changed to regional shepherd, with pay raised to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 建武十八年，复为刺史，十二人各主一州，其一州属司隶校尉。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jianwu they were again made inspectors, twelve men each in charge of one province; one province belonged to the Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 18 the office reverted to inspector; twelve men each governed one province, while the remaining province fell under the Colonel Director of Retainers at the capital.

sentences.zh: 蔡質漢儀曰：「詔書舊典，刺史班宣，周行郡國，省察治政，黜陟能否，斷理冤獄，以六條問事，非條所問，卽不省。

translations.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Observances says: "By the old canon of edicts, inspectors promulgated and proclaimed, toured the commanderies and kingdoms, inspected and examined governance, demoted or promoted according to ability, decided wrongful imprisonments, and investigated affairs by six articles; what fell outside the articles was not examined.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhi's Han Observances records: "By ancient edict, inspectors proclaimed imperial orders, toured commanderies and kingdoms, inspected governance, promoted or dismissed officials, redressed wrongful imprisonment, and investigated affairs under six articles; matters outside those articles were not pursued.

sentences.zh: 一條，強宗豪右，田宅踰制，以強陵弱，以衆暴寡。

translations.literal: Article one: powerful clans and great houses whose fields and dwellings exceeded regulations, using strength to bully the weak and numbers to oppress the few.
translations.idiomatic: Article one: powerful clans whose estates exceeded regulations, bullying the weak and oppressing the few.

sentences.zh: 二條，二千石不奉詔書，遵承典制，倍公向私，旁詔守利，侵漁百姓，聚斂爲姦。

translations.literal: Article two: two-thousand-picul officials who did not follow edicts, uphold canonical institutions, turned from public to private, sought profit on the side, preyed upon the people, and amassed wealth as treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Article two: grand administrators who defied edicts, pursued private gain, preyed on the people, and amassed wealth corruptly.

sentences.zh: 三條，二千石不卹疑獄，風厲殺人，怒則任刑，喜則任賞，煩擾苛暴，剝戮黎元，爲百姓所疾，山崩石裂，妖祥訛言。

translations.literal: Article three: two-thousand-picul officials who did not care for doubtful cases, encouraged killing, imposed punishments in anger and rewards in joy, were vexatious and cruel, flayed and slaughtered the people, were hated by the common folk, and were linked to omens such as mountain collapses, stone splits, and false prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Article three: grand administrators who ignored doubtful cases, killed recklessly, punished in anger and rewarded in joy, tormented the people, and were hated amid omens and false reports.

sentences.zh: 四條，二千石選署不平，苟阿所愛，蔽賢寵頑。

translations.literal: Article four: two-thousand-picul officials whose selections and appointments were unfair, who fawned on favorites, concealed the worthy, and pampered the obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: Article four: grand administrators who appointed unfairly, favored cronies, hid the worthy, and indulged the obstinate.

sentences.zh: 五條，二千石子弟怙恃榮勢，請託所監。

translations.literal: Article five: sons and younger brothers of two-thousand-picul officials who relied on glory and power and made requests through those they supervised.
translations.idiomatic: Article five: sons and younger brothers of grand administrators who abused their fathers' power to seek favors within the inspector's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 六條，二千石違公下比，阿附豪強，通行貨賂，割損政令。

translations.literal: Article six: two-thousand-picul officials who violated the public to curry favor below, flattered powerful houses, trafficked in bribes, and cut and damaged government orders.
translations.idiomatic: Article six: grand administrators who curried favor with the powerful, accepted bribes, and undermined government orders.

sentences.zh: 諸州刺史初除，比諸持板揖不拜。」

translations.literal: When provincial inspectors were first appointed, they were compared to those who held tablets and bowed without performing the full prostration."
translations.idiomatic: Newly appointed provincial inspectors bowed with tablet in hand without performing the full prostration."

sentences.zh: 獻帝起居注曰：「建安十八年三月庚寅，省州幷郡，復禹貢之九州。

translations.literal: The Daily Records of Emperor Xian say: "In the third month of the eighteenth year of Jian'an, on the day gengyin, provinces were merged and commanderies abolished, restoring the nine provinces of Yu's Tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian's Daily Records note: "In the third month of Jian'an 18, on gengyin, provinces were merged and commanderies cut to restore the nine provinces of Yu's Tribute.

sentences.zh: 冀州得魏郡、安平、鉅鹿、河閒、淸河、博陵、常山、趙國、勃海、甘陵、平原、太原、上黨、西河、定襄、鴈門、雲中、五原、朔方、河東、河内、涿郡、漁陽、廣陽、右北平、上谷、代郡、遼東、遼東屬國、遼西、玄菟、樂浪，凡三十二郡。

translations.literal: Jizhou received Wei, Anping, Julu, Hejian, Qinghe, Boling, Changshan, Zhao, Bohai, Ganling, Pingyuan, Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Dingxiang, Yanmen, Yunzhong, Wuyuan, Shuofang, Hedong, Henei, Zhuo, Yuyang, Guangyang, Right Beiping, Shanggu, Dai, Liaodong, Liaodong Dependent State, Liaoxi, Xuantu, and Lelang—thirty-two commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou absorbed thirty-two commanderies including Wei, Anping, Julu, Hejian, Qinghe, Boling, Changshan, Zhao, Bohai, Ganling, Pingyuan, Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Dingxiang, Yanmen, Yunzhong, Wuyuan, Shuofang, Hedong, Henei, Zhuo, Yuyang, Guangyang, Right Beiping, Shanggu, Dai, Liaodong, Liaodong Dependent State, Liaoxi, Xuantu, and Lelang.

sentences.zh: 省司隸校尉，以司隸部分屬豫州、冀州、雍州。

translations.literal: The Colonel Director of Retainers was abolished, and the metropolitan region was divided among Yuzhou, Jizhou, and Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel Director of Retainers was abolished and the metropolitan region was divided among Yuzhou, Jizhou, and Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 省涼州刺史，以幷雍州部，郡得弘農、京兆、左馮翊、右扶風、上郡、安定、隴西、漢陽、北地、武都、武威、金城、西平、西郡、張掖、張掖屬國、酒泉、敦煌、西海、漢興、永陽、東安南，凡二十二郡。

translations.literal: The inspector of Liangzhou was abolished and merged into Yongzhou; the commanderies were Hongnong, Jingzhao, Left Fengyi, Right Fufeng, Shang, Anding, Longxi, Hanyang, Beidi, Wudu, Wuwei, Jincheng, Xiping, Xijun, Zhangye, Zhangye Dependent State, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, Xihai, Hanxing, Yongyang, and Dong'annan—twenty-two commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou was abolished and merged into Yongzhou, comprising twenty-two commanderies from Hongnong and Jingzhao west through Dunhuang and the frontier districts.

sentences.zh: 省交州，以其郡屬荊州。

translations.literal: Jiaozhou was abolished and its commanderies placed under Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou was abolished and its commanderies transferred to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 荊州得交州之蒼梧、南海、九眞、交趾、日南，與其舊所部南陽、章陵、南郡、江夏、武陵、長沙、零陵、桂陽，凡十三〔郡〕。

translations.literal: Jingzhou received Cangwu, Nanhai, Jiuzhen, Jiaozhi, and Rinan from Jiaozhou, together with its former jurisdictions Nanyang, Zhangling, Nan, Jiangxia, Wuling, Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang—thirteen commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou absorbed Cangwu, Nanhai, Jiuzhen, Jiaozhi, and Rinan from the old Jiaozhou together with Nanyang, Zhangling, Nan, Jiangxia, Wuling, Changsha, Lingling, and Guiyang—thirteen commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 益州本部郡有廣漢、漢中、巴郡、犍爲、蜀郡、牂牁、越巂、益州、永昌、犍爲屬國、蜀郡屬國、廣漢屬國，今幷得交州之鬱林、合浦，凡十四〔郡〕。

translations.literal: Yizhou's original commanderies were Guanghan, Hanzhong, Ba, Qianwei, Shu, Zangke, Yuexi, Yizhou, Yongchang, Qianwei Dependent State, Shu Dependent State, and Guanghan Dependent State; it now also received Yulin and Hepu from Jiaozhou—fourteen commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou retained Guanghan, Hanzhong, Ba, Qianwei, Shu, Zangke, Yuexi, Yizhou, Yongchang, and the three dependent states, and also received Yulin and Hepu from Jiaozhou—fourteen commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 豫州部郡本有潁川、陳國、汝南、沛國、梁國、魯國，今幷得河南、滎陽都尉，凡八郡。

translations.literal: Yuzhou originally had Yingchuan, Chen, Runan, Pei, Liang, and Lu; it now also received Henan and the commandant of Xingyang—eight commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou originally comprised Yingchuan, Chen, Runan, Pei, Liang, and Lu and now also received Henan and the Xingyang commandant—eight commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 徐州部郡得下邳、廣陵、彭城、東海、琅邪、利城、城陽、東莞，凡八郡。

translations.literal: Xuzhou's commanderies were Xiapi, Guangling, Pengcheng, Donghai, Langye, Licheng, Chengyang, and Dongguan—eight commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou comprised Xiapi, Guangling, Pengcheng, Donghai, Langye, Licheng, Chengyang, and Dongguan—eight commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 靑州得齊國、北海、東萊、濟南、樂安，凡五郡。」

translations.literal: Qingzhou received Qi, Beihai, Donglai, Jinan, and Le'an—five commanderies in all."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou comprised Qi, Beihai, Donglai, Jinan, and Le'an—five commanderies in all."

sentences.zh: 獻帝春秋曰：「孫權以歩騭行交州刺史。」

translations.literal: Chronicle of Emperor Xian says: "Sun Quan had Bu Zhi act as inspector of Jiaozhou."
translations.idiomatic: The Chronicle of Emperor Xian records: "Sun Quan had Bu Zhi serve as acting inspector of Jiaozhou."

sentences.zh: 東觀書曰：「交趾刺史，持節。」

translations.literal: Book of the Eastern Lodge says: "The inspector of Jiaozhi held the staff of authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of the Eastern Lodge notes: "The inspector of Jiaozhi bore the credential staff."

sentences.zh: 諸州常以八月巡行所部郡國，胡廣注曰：「巡謂驛馬也。

translations.literal: The provinces regularly in the eighth month toured the commanderies and kingdoms under their jurisdiction. Hu Guang annotates: "Touring means relay horses.
translations.idiomatic: Each province customarily made an autumn circuit of its commanderies and kingdoms. Hu Guang explains: "The tour used relay horses.

sentences.zh: 縣次傳駕之，以走疾，猶古言附遂。」

translations.literal: At each county stop relay teams drove them, running swiftly, as in the ancient phrase 'attached relay.'"
translations.idiomatic: At each county relay teams drove them at speed, as in the ancient term for attached relay transport."

sentences.zh: 録囚徒，胡廣曰：「縣邑囚徒，皆閲録視，參考辭狀，實其眞偽。

translations.literal: They reviewed prisoners. Hu Guang says: "Prisoners in counties and districts were all examined and reviewed, with testimony checked to verify truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: They reviewed prisoners. Hu Guang says: "County prisoners were examined, testimony checked, and truth verified.

sentences.zh: 有侵冤者，卽時平理也。」

translations.literal: Where there was oppression or injustice, it was promptly redressed."
translations.idiomatic: Cases of oppression or injustice were promptly redressed."

sentences.zh: 考殿最。

translations.literal: They assessed best and worst performance.
translations.idiomatic: They rated administrative performance.

sentences.zh: 胡廣曰：「課第長吏不稱職者爲殿，舉免之。

translations.literal: Hu Guang says: "In ranking officials, those unfit for office were rated 'lowest' and recommended for dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang says: "Officials ranked lowest for incompetence were recommended for dismissal.

sentences.zh: 其有治能者爲最。

translations.literal: Those with governing ability were rated 'best.'
translations.idiomatic: Those with governing ability were rated best.

sentences.zh: 察上尤異州，又狀州中吏民茂才異等，歳舉一人。」

translations.literal: Outstanding cases were reported upward; the inspector also presented men of outstanding talent and special distinction among officials and people of the province, one man recommended each year."
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding cases were reported upward, and one man of special talent among the province's officials and people was recommended each year."

sentences.zh: 初歳盡詣京都奏事，胡廣曰：「所察有條應繩異者，輒覆問之，不茹柔吐剛也。

translations.literal: At first at year's end they went to the capital to report affairs. Hu Guang says: "Where what they inspected had items that should be bound by rule or were unusual, they were questioned again; they did not swallow the soft and spit out the hard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, inspectors journeyed to the capital at year's end to report. Hu Guang says: "Doubtful or unusual findings were reinvestigated; they did not favor the weak over the strong.

sentences.zh: 歳盡，齎所狀納京師，名奏事，差其遠近，各有常會。」

translations.literal: At year's end they brought their reports to the capital, called 'reporting affairs,' with distances graded and fixed schedules for each."
translations.idiomatic: At year's end they carried their reports to the capital—called reporting affairs—with fixed schedules according to distance."

sentences.zh: 中興但因計吏。

translations.literal: In the restoration they relied only on the accounting clerks.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration this duty devolved on the accounting clerks who came up with the tribute tallies.

sentences.zh: 胡廣曰：「不復自詣京師，其所道皆如舊典。」

translations.literal: Hu Guang says: "They no longer went in person to the capital; what they transmitted followed the old canon."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang adds: "Inspectors no longer went in person; their reports followed the old canon."

sentences.zh: 東觀書曰：「和帝初，張酺上言：『臣聞王者法天，熒惑奏事太微，故州牧刺史入奏事，所以通下問知外事也。

translations.literal: The Book of the Eastern Lodge says: "Early in Emperor He, Zhang Ti memorialized: 'I have heard that kings model Heaven; Mars reports affairs in the Supreme Palace Enclosure, therefore regional shepherds and inspectors enter to report affairs so as to connect below and learn of outer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of the Eastern Lodge records: "Early in Emperor He's reign Zhang Ti memorialized: 'The king models Heaven; Mars reports in the Supreme Palace Enclosure, so regional shepherds and inspectors reported at court to learn of distant affairs.

sentences.zh: 數十年以來，重其道歸煩撓，故時止勿奏事，今因以爲故事。

translations.literal: For several decades the burden of their journeys caused trouble and annoyance, so at times reporting was stopped; now this has become precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For decades the journey burdened the court, so reporting was suspended and that suspension became precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲刺史視事滿歳，可令奏事如舊典，問州中風俗，恐好惡過所道，事所聞見，考課衆職，下章所告，及所自舉有意者賞異之，其尤無狀，逆詔書，行罪法，冀敕戒其餘，令各敬愼所職，於以衰滅貪邪便佞。』」

translations.literal: I foolishly think that when an inspector has completed a full year in office, he may be ordered to report as in the old canon, inquiring into customs of the province, fearing that likes and dislikes exceed what is reported and that matters seen and heard are not conveyed; examining and assessing all offices; rewarding with distinction those reported below or self-recommended with merit; punishing by law those utterly without propriety who defy edicts, hoping to admonish the rest and make each reverently careful in his post, thereby to diminish greedy, wicked, and fawning men.'"
translations.idiomatic: I propose that after a full year in office inspectors resume reporting as of old—inquiring into provincial customs, reviewing all offices, rewarding merit, and punishing those who defy edicts, so the rest may be admonished and greedy flatterers diminished.'"

sentences.zh: 韓詩外傳曰：「王者必立牧，方三人，所以使闚遠牧衆也。

translations.literal: Han Ying's Outer Commentary on the Odes says: "Kings must establish shepherds, three for each direction, in order to observe from afar and shepherd the multitudes.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ying's Outer Commentary on the Odes says: "Kings must appoint shepherds—three for each direction—to watch from afar and govern the people.

sentences.zh: 遠方之民，有飢寒而不得衣食，獄訟而冤失，職賢而不舉者，入告天子。

translations.literal: Among distant peoples, if there were hunger and cold without food and clothing, lawsuits with wrongful loss, or worthy men in office not recommended, they entered to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If distant peoples suffered hunger, wrongful imprisonment, or failure to recommend the worthy, the shepherd reported to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天子於其君之朝也，揖而進之曰：『意朕之政教，有不得爾者邪？

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven was at that lord's court, he bowed and advanced him, saying: 'Do you think my government and teaching have failed you in some way?
translations.idiomatic: At that lord's audience the Son of Heaven bowed him forward and asked: 'Do you think my government has failed you?

sentences.zh: 如何乃有飢寒而不得衣食，獄訟而冤失，職賢而不舉？』

translations.literal: How is it that there are hunger and cold without food and clothing, lawsuits with wrongful loss, and worthy men in office not recommended?'
translations.idiomatic: How then are there hunger and cold, wrongful lawsuits, and failure to recommend the worthy?'

sentences.zh: 然後其君退而與其卿大夫謀之。

translations.literal: Then that lord withdrew and deliberated with his ministers and grandees.
translations.idiomatic: The lord then withdrew to consult his ministers and grandees.

sentences.zh: 遠方之民聞，皆曰『誠天子也』。

translations.literal: When distant peoples heard, all said, 'Truly a Son of Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, distant peoples said, 'Truly a Son of Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 夫我居之辟，見我之近也；

translations.literal: Though I dwell in seclusion, he sees me as near;
translations.idiomatic: Though I dwell afar, he sees me as near;

sentences.zh: 我居之幽，見我之明也。

translations.literal: though I dwell in obscurity, he sees me as bright.
translations.idiomatic: though I dwell in obscurity, he sees me as bright.

sentences.zh: 可欺乎哉！

translations.literal: Can one be deceived!
translations.idiomatic: Can one be deceived!

sentences.zh: 可欺乎哉！

translations.literal: Can one be deceived!
translations.idiomatic: Can one be deceived!

sentences.zh: 故牧者所以開四目，通四聰。」

translations.literal: Therefore shepherds are what open the four eyes and connect the four ears."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore shepherds open the four eyes and connect the four ears of the ruler."

sentences.zh: 皆有从事史、假佐。

translations.literal: All had attendant clerks and acting assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Each staff included attendant secretaries and provisional aides.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：员职略与司隶同，无都官从事，其功曹从事为治中从事。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The posts were broadly the same as under the Colonel Director of Retainers, but without a capital-crimes attendant; the merit-clerk attendant was called the attendant for internal administration.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The complement mirrored that of the Colonel Director of Retainers, except that there was no attendant for capital cases; the merit-clerk attendant was titled attendant for internal administration.

sentences.zh: 豫州部郡国六，冀州部九，兗州部八，徐州部五，青州部六，荆州部七，扬州部六，益州部十二，凉州部十二，并州部九，幽州部十一，交州部七，凡九十八。

translations.literal: Yuzhou supervised six commanderies and kingdoms; Jizhou nine; Yanzhou eight; Xuzhou five; Qingzhou six; Jingzhou seven; Yangzhou six; Yizhou twelve; Liangzhou twelve; Bingzhou nine; Youzhou eleven; Jiaozhou seven; in all ninety-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou oversaw six commanderies and kingdoms; Jizhou nine; Yanzhou eight; Xuzhou five; Qingzhou six; Jingzhou seven; Yangzhou six; Yizhou twelve; Liangzhou twelve; Bingzhou nine; Youzhou eleven; Jiaozhou seven—ninety-eight units in all.

sentences.zh: 其二十七王国相，其七十一郡太守。

translations.literal: Of these twenty-seven were chancellors of princely kingdoms; seventy-one were grand administrators of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven were chancellors serving princely fiefs; seventy-one were grand administrators of ordinary commanderies.

sentences.zh: 其属国都尉。

translations.literal: There were also chief commandants of dependent states.
translations.idiomatic: Dependent states were headed by chief commandants as well.

sentences.zh: 属国，分郡离远县置之，如郡差小，置本郡名。

translations.literal: Dependent states were set up by splitting off remote counties from a commandery; they were slightly smaller than a commandery and kept the parent commandery’s name.
translations.idiomatic: A dependent state was carved from outlying counties of a commandery; it was somewhat smaller than a full commandery and usually retained the original commandery designation.

sentences.zh: 世祖并省郡县四百余所，后世稍复增之。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu merged and abolished more than four hundred commanderies and counties; later ages gradually restored some.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor merged away over four hundred commanderies and counties; succeeding reigns slowly added others back.

sentences.zh: 臣昭曰：昔在先代，列爵殊等，九服不同，畿荒制異。

translations.literal: Chen Zhao says: In former ages, ranks of nobility differed in grade; the nine domains were not alike; the regulations of the metropolitan region and the wild borderlands differed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhao writes: In antiquity noble ranks were graded, the nine service zones followed distinct rules, and metropolitan and frontier administrations differed in form.

sentences.zh: 雖連帥相司，牧伯分長，而封疆置限，兼庸有數，如身之使臂，手之使指，故能髙卑相固，遠近維緝，群後克穆，共康兆庶。

translations.literal: Although connected commanders supervised one another and regional shepherds and earls divided authority, yet territorial limits were set and attached domains had fixed numbers, like the body commanding the arm and the hand commanding the fingers; thus high and low were mutually secured, far and near were bound together, the feudal lords were harmonious, and together they brought peace to the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Though overlords and regional shepherds shared governance, borders were fixed and subordinate holdings numbered, like arm and finger—high and low reinforced one another, near and far were knit together, and the feudal lords jointly secured the people.

sentences.zh: 爰及周衰，稍競呑廣，邦國侵爭，遞懷貪略，猶歴數百年，乃能成其幷一，豈非樹之有本，使其然乎？

translations.literal: When Zhou declined, they gradually competed to swallow and expand; states invaded and fought one another, each in turn harboring greedy designs; only after several hundred years could unity be achieved—is this not because a tree has roots that make it so?
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou decayed, states swallowed one another in greedy wars; centuries passed before unity returned—did not deep roots make that possible?

sentences.zh: 秦兼天下，開設郡縣，孤立獨王，卽以顛亡。

translations.literal: Qin united the realm, established commanderies and counties, isolated the sole king, and thereby toppled and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Qin conquered all under Heaven, imposed commanderies and counties, left the emperor isolated—and swiftly fell.

sentences.zh: 漢祖因循，雖不頓革，分置子弟，終龕諸呂之難，漸剖列郡，以減大都之權。

translations.literal: The Han founder followed precedent; though he did not reform all at once, he enfeoffed sons and younger brothers, yet in the end encountered the disaster of the Lü clan; he gradually carved out commanderies to reduce the power of great metropolises.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu kept much of the old order yet enfeoffed kin; still the Lü crisis erupted, and the court slowly split great domains to curb metropolitan power.

sentences.zh: 後嚴安之徒，猶慷慨發憤，謂千里之威，卽古之強國，慮非安本無窮之計也。

translations.literal: Later men like Yan An still spoke with indignant passion, saying that authority over a thousand li was already the strength of an ancient great state, and fearing this was not a plan to secure the root for endless peace.
translations.idiomatic: Later critics such as Yan An protested that a thousand-li jurisdiction equaled an ancient great power and warned that such scale could not secure the dynasty forever.

sentences.zh: 孝武之末，始置刺史，監糾非法，不過六條，傳車周流，匪有定鎭，秩裁數百，威望輕寡，得有察舉之勤，未生陵犯之釁。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Wu, inspectors were first established to oversee and correct illegal acts, limited to six articles; relay carriages circulated without a fixed seat; rank was only several hundred piculs; prestige was light and thin; they could perform the diligence of inspection and recommendation without giving rise to the omen of encroachment and violation.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Wu's reign inspectors were introduced to police misconduct under six articles; they toured by relay carriage without fixed headquarters, held modest rank, and could investigate without yet threatening commandery power.

sentences.zh: 成帝改牧，其萌始大，旣非識治之主，故無取焉爾。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng changed them to regional shepherds; the sprout then grew large; since he was not a ruler who understood governance, there is nothing to approve in this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng elevated them to regional shepherds and the office swelled; he was no master of statecraft, so the change merits no praise.

sentences.zh: 世祖中興，監乎政本，復約其職，還遵舊制，斷親奏事，省入惜煩，漸得自重之路。

translations.literal: The founding emperor in the restoration watched the root of government, again reduced their duties, returned to the old system, cut off personal attendance to report affairs, spared the capital trouble and annoyance, and gradually gained a path to renewed weight.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu, restoring the dynasty, trimmed the office back to the old inspector model, ended personal reporting at court, and thereby gave the post a path to renewed authority.

sentences.zh: 因茲以降，彌於歳年，母后當朝，多以弱守，六合危動，四海潰弊，財盡力竭，綱維撓毀，而八方不能内侵，諸侯莫敢入伐，豈非幹強枝弱，控制素重之所致乎？

translations.literal: From this downward through the years, empress dowagers often held court and mostly ruled through weakness; the six directions trembled in peril, the four seas collapsed in exhaustion, wealth was spent and strength drained, the guiding net was bent and broken—yet the eight directions could not invade inward and feudal lords dared not enter to attack; was this not caused by a strong trunk and weak branches and by control that had long been heavy?
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter empress dowagers often reigned from weakness while the realm tottered; treasury and strength failed and institutions frayed—yet outsiders did not invade and princes dared not rebel. Was this not because the center stayed strong while branches were kept weak?

sentences.zh: 至孝靈在位，橫流旣及，劉焉徼偽，自爲身謀，非有憂國之心，專懷狼據之策，抗論昏世，薦議愚主，盛稱宜重牧伯，謂足鎭壓萬里，挾姦樹筭，苟罔一時，豈可永爲國本，長期勝術哉？

translations.literal: When Emperor Ling reigned, the flood had already arrived; Liu Yan sought false credit for his own designs, not with a heart that worried for the state but harboring a wolfish strategy of seizure; he argued against a benighted age and recommended to a foolish sovereign, loudly praising the need to strengthen regional shepherds, saying they could suppress ten thousand li; clutching treachery and planting schemes, he deceived for a moment—how could this forever be the foundation of the state or a long-term winning strategy?
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling, Liu Yan schemed for himself, not the realm, urging heavier regional shepherds to control ten thousand li—a treacherous expedient, not a lasting foundation of state.

sentences.zh: 夫聖主御世，莫不大庇生民，承其休謀，傳其典制。

translations.literal: Sage rulers who govern the age all greatly shelter the living people, inherit their excellent plans, and transmit their canonical institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers shelter the people, inherit sound policy, and pass down established institutions.

sentences.zh: 猶雲事久獘生，無或通貫，故變改正服，革異質文，分爵三五，參差不一。

translations.literal: Yet it is said that when affairs grow old, decay arises and none can fully penetrate; therefore they changed and corrected robes, altered substance and pattern, divided ranks into threes and fives, uneven and not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, institutions age and decay; hence robes, rites, and noble ranks were repeatedly revised and never uniform.

sentences.zh: 況在豎騃之君，挾姦詐之臣，共所創置，焉可仍因？

translations.literal: How much less when childish and foolish rulers, together with treacherous and deceitful ministers, jointly created institutions—how could these simply be continued?
translations.idiomatic: How much less should the creations of foolish rulers and scheming ministers be perpetuated unchanged?

sentences.zh: 大建尊州之規，竟無一日之治。

translations.literal: They greatly built the scheme of exalted provinces, yet not one day of good order resulted.
translations.idiomatic: The grand project of exalted provinces produced not a single day of good government.

sentences.zh: 故焉牧益土，造帝服於岷、峨；

translations.literal: Thus when Yi became shepherd he enlarged territory and fashioned imperial robes at Min and E;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan as regional shepherd expanded his domain and donned imperial regalia in the Min-E region;

sentences.zh: 袁紹取冀，下制書於燕、朔；

translations.literal: Yuan Shao took Ji and issued edicts in Yan and Shuo;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao seized Ji and issued edicts across Yan and the northern frontier;

sentences.zh: 劉表荊南，郊天祀地；

translations.literal: Liu Biao in southern Jing performed suburban sacrifices to Heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao in southern Jing performed suburban rites to Heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 魏祖據兗，遂構皇業：漢之殄滅，禍源乎此。

translations.literal: Cao the Wei founder held Yan and then built an imperial enterprise: the extinction of Han had its source in this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao held Yan and built an imperial enterprise—the extinction of Han began here.

sentences.zh: 及臻後代，任寄彌廣，委之邦宰之命，授之斧鉞之重，假之都督之威，開之征討之略。

translations.literal: When later ages arrived, commissions grew ever broader: they entrusted the mandate of territorial governors, conferred the weight of battle-axes, lent the authority of regional commissioners, and opened the strategy of punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages widened provincial commissions—territorial command, military authority, regional commissioners, and punitive campaigns.

sentences.zh: 晉太康之初，武帝亦疑其然，乃詔曰：「上古及中代，或置州牧，或置刺史，置監御史，皆總綱紀，而不賦政，治民之事，任之諸侯郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang in Jin, Emperor Wu also doubted that this was right, and issued an edict saying: "In high antiquity and the middle ages, sometimes regional shepherds were placed, sometimes inspectors, sometimes supervising clerks; all oversaw the guiding net but did not levy government; matters of governing the people were entrusted to feudal lords and commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin Taikang, Emperor Wu also doubted the trend and decreed: "In antiquity and the middle ages, regional shepherds, inspectors, or supervising clerks oversaw discipline but did not govern the people; that duty belonged to feudal lords and commandery governors.

sentences.zh: 昔漢末四海分崩，因以呉、蜀自擅，自是刺史内親民事，外領兵馬，此一時之宜爾。

translations.literal: Formerly at the end of Han the four seas split apart, and Wu and Shu accordingly seized power for themselves; from then inspectors personally handled civil affairs within and commanded troops and horses without—this was a temporary expedient.
translations.idiomatic: When Han fell, Wu and Shu seized power and inspectors took civil and military duties—a temporary expedient.

sentences.zh: 今賴宗廟之靈，士大夫之力，江表平定，天下合之爲一，當韜戢干戈，與天下休息。

translations.literal: Now relying on the spirit of the ancestral temple and the strength of scholar-officials, the lands south of the river are pacified and all under Heaven are united as one; we should sheath weapons and let the realm rest.
translations.idiomatic: Now, with the south pacified and the realm reunited, arms should be sheathed and the people allowed to rest.

sentences.zh: 諸州無事者罷其兵，刺史分職，皆如漢氏故事，出頒詔條，入奏事京城。

translations.literal: Provinces without emergency should disband their troops; inspectors should divide duties all according to Han precedent, going out to promulgate edicts and coming in to report affairs at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Peaceful provinces should disband troops; inspectors should resume Han practice—promulgating edicts abroad and reporting at the capital.

sentences.zh: 二千石專治民之重，監司淸峻於上，此經久之體也。

translations.literal: The two-thousand-picul officials should exclusively bear the weight of governing the people, while supervising offices remain stern and lofty above—this is the enduring structure.
translations.idiomatic: Grand administrators should govern the people while inspectors remain stern overseers above—this is the lasting order.

sentences.zh: 其便省州牧。」

translations.literal: Let regional shepherds be abolished for convenience."
translations.idiomatic: Regional shepherds should therefore be abolished."

sentences.zh: 晉武帝又見其獘矣，雖有其言，不卒其事，後嗣纘繼，牧鎭愈重，據地分爭，竟覆天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin again saw its decay; though he had these words, he did not complete the matter; later successors continued, regional shepherds and garrisons grew heavier, seized territory and fought for division, and in the end overturned the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin saw the danger but did not finish the reform; successors made regional shepherds and garrisons heavier until partition overturned the realm.

sentences.zh: 昔王畿之大，不過千里，州之所司，廣袤兼遠。

translations.literal: Formerly the metropolitan region was no more than a thousand li in extent, yet what a province administered was vast in breadth and far in distance.
translations.idiomatic: Once the royal domain spanned barely a thousand li, yet a province might govern vastly more.

sentences.zh: 爭強虎視之辰，遷鼎革終之日，未嘗不藉蕃兵之權，挾董司之力，逼迫伺隙，陵奪沖幼。

translations.literal: In times when rivals glared like tigers and the tripods were moved at the end of a dynasty, never did they fail to rely on the authority of frontier troops and wield the power of provincial commissioners, pressing hard and watching for openings, encroaching upon and seizing the young and weak.
translations.idiomatic: In ages of fierce rivalry and dynastic collapse, men always leaned on frontier armies and provincial commissioners to press weaknesses and seize the young.

sentences.zh: 其甚者臣主揚兵，骨肉戰野，昆弟梟懸，伯叔屠裂。

translations.literal: At the extreme, ministers and rulers raised armies; flesh and blood battled in the wilds; brothers were displayed on poles; uncles were torn apart.
translations.idiomatic: At worst, lord and minister took up arms, kin slaughtered kin, brothers were displayed on poles, and uncles were torn apart.

sentences.zh: 末壯披心，尾大不掉，旣用此始，亦病以終。

translations.literal: When the tip grows strong it splits the heart; when the tail grows large it cannot be shaken off—this was both how it began and how it ended in sickness.
translations.idiomatic: The branch grew strong enough to split the trunk and the tail too heavy to wag—so the disease began and so it ended.

sentences.zh: 傾輈愈襲，莫或途改，致雒京有銜璧之痛，秦臺有不守之酷。

translations.literal: Overturning and collision were ever repeated; none changed course on the road, bringing the agony of jade held between the teeth at Luoyang and the cruelty of the Qin terrace undefended.
translations.idiomatic: Reversals piled on reversals until none changed course—Luoyang knew the agony of surrender and the Qin terrace fell undefended.

sentences.zh: 胡、羌遞興，氐、鮮更起，摩滅群黎，流禍百世。

translations.literal: Hu and Qiang rose in succession; Di and Xianbei arose again; they ground down the multitudes and spread calamity for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, Qiang, Di, and Xianbei rose in turn, grinding down the people and spreading calamity for generations.

sentences.zh: 堅冰所漸，兼縁茲蠹。

translations.literal: Hard ice forms by gradual freezing; this pestilence too had its gradual cause.
translations.idiomatic: Hard ice forms by degrees—and this rot had long been gathering.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 後之聖王，必不久滯斯跡，靈長之終，當有神筭。

translations.literal: Later sage kings will surely not long linger on this path; at the end of enduring fortune there ought to be a divine reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Later sage kings will not long follow this path; enduring fortune should end in providential correction.

sentences.zh: 不然，則雄捍反拒之事，懼甚於此心，憑強作害之謀，方盛於後意。

translations.literal: If not, then deeds of fierce defiance and resistance will inspire fear greater than this present mind, and schemes to rely on strength and do harm will flourish still more in later intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise defiance born of strength will breed greater fear, and plots to harm by force will grow still worse.

sentences.zh: 凡州所监都为京都，置尹一人，二千石，丞一人，每郡置太守一人，二千石，丞一人。

translations.literal: In general, wherever a province supervised the capital district as its metropolis, one intendant was appointed at two thousand piculs and one assistant; each commandery had one grand administrator at two thousand piculs and one assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Where a province’s seat of supervision was the capital region, a single metropolitan intendant at two thousand piculs and one deputy were appointed; elsewhere each commandery had one grand administrator at two thousand piculs and one assistant.

sentences.zh: 郡当边戍者，丞为长史。

translations.literal: Commanderies on the frontier for garrison duty made the assistant a chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: On border commanderies charged with defense, the assistant was redesignated chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 王国之相亦如之。

translations.literal: The chancellors of princely kingdoms were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors of princely kingdoms followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 每属国置都尉一人，比二千石，丞一人。

translations.literal: Each dependent state had one chief commandant, comparable to two thousand piculs, and one assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Each dependent state placed one chief commandant at the “comparable to two thousand piculs” grade, plus a single assistant.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：凡郡國皆掌治民，進賢勸功，決訟檢奸。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In general commanderies and kingdoms governed the people, advanced the worthy, urged achievement, decided lawsuits, and checked wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Commanderies and kingdoms were responsible for governing the populace, recommending talent, encouraging good service, adjudicating litigation, and suppressing crime.

sentences.zh: 常以春行所主縣，勸民農桑，振救乏絶。

translations.literal: They regularly in spring toured the counties under their charge, urging farming and sericulture, and relieving those in want.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring they made a circuit of subordinate counties to promote agriculture and silk production and to aid the destitute.

sentences.zh: 秋冬遣無害吏案訊諸囚，平其罪法，論課殿最。

translations.literal: In autumn and winter they sent harmless clerks to interrogate all prisoners, balance penalties according to law, and assess best and worst.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn and winter they dispatched incorruptible subordinates to review prisoners, align sentences with the code, and grade performance.

sentences.zh: 案律有無害都吏，如今言公平吏。

translations.literal: According to the code there were incorrupt capital clerks, as one now speaks of fair-minded officers.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes mention incorrupt capital clerks—the same sort later called fair-minded officers.

sentences.zh: 漢書音義曰：「文無所枉害。」

translations.literal: The Sounds and Meanings of the History of Han says: "In documents there was nothing warped or harmed."
translations.idiomatic: The Sounds and Meanings of the History of Han glosses the phrase as "in documents nothing was twisted or wronged."

sentences.zh: 蕭何以文無害爲沛主吏掾。

translations.literal: Xiao He served as chief clerk of Pei because his documents were incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He won appointment as chief clerk of Pei on the strength of his incorrupt record-keeping.

sentences.zh: 岁尽遣吏上计。

translations.literal: At year’s end they sent clerks up with the annual accounts.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the year clerks carried the annual accounts to their superiors.

sentences.zh: 并举孝廉，郡口二十万举一人。

translations.literal: They also recommended filial and incorrupt candidates; for every two hundred thousand mouths in the commandery one man was recommended.
translations.idiomatic: They nominated candidates for the filial-and-incorrupt quota at the rate of one man per two hundred thousand registered persons.

sentences.zh: 尉一人，典兵禁，备盗贼，景帝更名都尉。

translations.literal: One commandant, in charge of troops and prohibitions, guarding against bandits; Emperor Jing changed the name to commandant.
translations.idiomatic: A commandant oversaw military readiness and police functions; Emperor Jing renamed the post commandant of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 武帝又置三辅都尉各一人，讥出入。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also placed one metropolitan commandant in each of the three adjunct capitals, to regulate entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu further assigned one commandant to each of the three capital adjuncts to control traffic in and out of those regions.

sentences.zh: 边郡置农都尉，主屯田殖谷。

translations.literal: Border commanderies set agricultural commandants in charge of garrison fields and grain increase.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanderies appointed agricultural commandants to manage military colonies and grain production.

sentences.zh: 又置属国都尉，主蛮夷降者。

translations.literal: They also set chief commandants of dependent states in charge of surrendered barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chief commandants of dependent states were added to administer surrendered non-Chinese peoples.

sentences.zh: 中兴建武六年，省诸郡都尉，并职太守，无都试之役。

translations.literal: In the restoration, the sixth year of Jianwu, all commandery commandants were abolished and their duties merged with the grand administrator; there were no more general musters.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, in Jianwu 6, commandery-level commandants were eliminated and their powers folded into the grand administrator’s office, ending the empire-wide autumn drills.

sentences.zh: 省关都尉，唯边郡往往置都尉及属国都尉，稍有分县，治民比郡。

translations.literal: The pass commandants were abolished; only border commanderies commonly retained commandants and chief commandants of dependent states, sometimes with divided counties, governing people on a par with a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Interior pass commandants were dropped; frontier areas often kept commandants and dependent-state commandants, sometimes with split counties whose magistrates ruled populations comparable to a full commandery.

sentences.zh: 安帝以羌犯法，三辅有陵园之守，乃复置右扶风都尉，京兆虎牙都尉。

translations.literal: Emperor An, because the Qiang broke the law and the three adjuncts guarded imperial tombs, again set a commandant of Right Fufeng and a “tiger-teeth” commandant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang revolted and the three adjuncts had to secure the imperial mausolea, Emperor An restored the Right Fufeng commandant and the Jingzhao “tiger-teeth” commandant.

sentences.zh: 應劭漢官曰：「蓋天生五材，民並用之，廢一不可，誰能去兵？

translations.literal: Ying Shao's Han Offices says: "Heaven produced the five materials and the people all use them; to abolish one is impossible—who can dispense with arms?
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Han Offices argues: "Heaven gave the five materials for common use; none can be discarded—who can abolish the military?

sentences.zh: 兵之設尙矣。

translations.literal: The establishment of arms is ancient indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The institution of arms is very old.

sentences.zh: 易稱『絃木爲弧，剡木爲矢，弧矢之利，以威天下。』

translations.literal: The Changes says, "Bend wood for a bow, carve wood for arrows; the advantage of bow and arrow is to awe all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Bend wood into a bow and carve wood into arrows; bow and arrow awe the realm."

sentences.zh: 春秋『三時務農，一時講武』。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals says, "Three seasons for farming, one season for military drill."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn tradition holds, "Three seasons for agriculture, one for martial training."

sentences.zh: 詩美公劉『匪居匪康，入耕出戰，乃裹餱糧，干戈載

translations.literal: The Odes praise Duke Liu: "Neither dwelling at ease nor living in comfort, going out to plow and going forth to battle, wrapping dry provisions, weapons borne
translations.idiomatic: The Odes praise Duke Liu: "Not idle, not at ease—farming in peace and fighting in war, packing dry rations, bearing arms

translations.idiomatic: (Xi)

sentences.zh: 〔揚〕，四方莫當』。

translations.literal: [Yang], none in the four quarters could withstand him."
translations.idiomatic: [raised aloft], and none in the four quarters could stand against him."

sentences.zh: 自郡國罷材官騎士之後，官無警備，實啓寇心。

translations.literal: After commanderies and kingdoms abolished materiel officers and cavalrymen, the offices had no guard preparations and truly opened the way to bandit hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Once commanderies disbanded materiel officers and cavalry, local governments lost their guard and truly invited raiders.

sentences.zh: 一方有難，三面救之，發興雷震，煙蒸電激，一切取辨，黔首囂然。

translations.literal: When one quarter had trouble, three sides rushed to rescue; mobilization thundered like lightning, smoke steamed and sparks flew; everything had to be improvised on the spot, and the black-headed people were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble struck one sector, three others scrambled to help; mobilization crashed like thunder while everything was improvised on the spot and the common people fell into uproar.

sentences.zh: 不及講其射御，用其戒誓，一旦驅之以卽強敵，猶鳩鵲捕鷹鸇，豚羊弋豺虎，是以毎戰常負，王旅不振。

translations.literal: There was no time to teach archery and charioteering or to use the oaths of warning; driving men at once against strong enemies was like doves and magpies hunting hawks and kites, or pigs and sheep shooting at wolves and tigers—hence every battle was usually lost and the royal host could not recover its vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Without time to drill archery and chariotry or renew battle oaths, hurling raw levies against hardened foes was like sending doves after hawks or pigs against tigers—battle after battle was lost and imperial forces could not recover.

sentences.zh: 張角懷挾妖偽，遐邇搖蕩，八州幷發，煙炎絳天，牧守梟裂，流血成川。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiao harbored demonic fraud; far and near were shaken; eight provinces erupted together; smoke and flame reddened the sky; regional shepherds and guardians were beheaded and torn apart; blood flowed like rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiao spread demonic fraud; the realm shook; eight provinces rose together; smoke reddened the sky; governors were slaughtered and blood ran like rivers.

sentences.zh: 爾乃遠徴三邊殊俗之兵，非我族類，忿鷙縱橫，多殭良善，以爲己功，財貨糞土。

translations.literal: Then they conscripted from afar soldiers of the three frontiers and alien customs—not our own kind—fierce and unrestrained, coercing many good people and counting it as their own merit, treating wealth like dung.
translations.idiomatic: Then distant frontier levies of alien custom—not our own people—were summoned; brutal and unchecked, they pressed good folk into service for private credit and treated wealth like refuse.

sentences.zh: 哀夫民氓遷流之咎，見出在茲，不教而戰，是謂棄之，跡其禍敗，豈虚也哉！

translations.literal: Alas for the blame of the people's wandering displacement—the cause appears here; to fight without teaching is called abandoning them; tracing their disaster and defeat, how could it be empty!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the roots of mass displacement lie here; sending untrained men to battle is abandonment; trace the ruin and the lesson is no empty warning!

sentences.zh: 春秋家不藏甲，所以一國威抑私力也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn tradition says households do not store armor, thereby unifying the state's authority and restraining private force.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn rule that households keep no armor unifies state authority and curbs private violence.

sentences.zh: 今雖四海殘壤，王命未洽，可折衝壓難，若指於掌，故置右扶風。」

translations.literal: Although the four seas are now broken ground and the king's command is not yet harmonized, one can break the enemy's charge and press down difficulty as if pointing on the palm—therefore Right Fufeng was established."
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm lies in ruins and royal authority is not yet secure, defense can still be managed at hand—hence the restoration of Right Fufeng commandant."

sentences.zh: 皆置诸曹掾史。

translations.literal: All established various bureau clerks and secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Each administration staffed the usual bureaus with clerks and secretaries.

sentences.zh: 新論曰：「王莽時置西海郡，令其吏皆百石親事。」

translations.literal: The New Discourses says: "When Wang Mang established Xihai commandery, he made its clerks all serve in person at the one-hundred-picul grade."
translations.idiomatic: The New Discourses says: "When Wang Mang created Xihai commandery, every clerk there served in person at the one-hundred-picul grade."

sentences.zh: 一曰爲四百石，二歳而遷補。

translations.literal: One account says they were at four hundred piculs and were transferred and replenished every two years.
translations.idiomatic: Another account makes the grade four hundred piculs, with rotation and replacement every two years.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：诸曹略如公府曹，无东西曹。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The bureaus were roughly like those of the Excellencies’ offices, but without east and west bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The bureau system paralleled the central ministries, minus the eastern and western personnel offices.

sentences.zh: 有功曹史，主选署功劳。

translations.literal: There was a merit-clerk secretary in charge of appointments and recording merit.
translations.idiomatic: A merit-clerk secretary handled selections and service records.

sentences.zh: 有五官掾，署功曹及诸曹事。

translations.literal: There was a steward of the five bureaus who supervised the merit clerk and the other bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: A steward of the five bureaus oversaw the merit office and the remaining bureaus.

sentences.zh: 其监属县，有五部督邮，曹掾一人。

translations.literal: For supervision of subordinate counties there were five route inspectors, one bureau clerk each.
translations.idiomatic: Five route inspectors watched the dependent counties, each supported by a bureau clerk.

sentences.zh: 正门有亭长一人。

translations.literal: At the main gate there was one ward head.
translations.idiomatic: The main gate was guarded by a single ward head.

sentences.zh: 主记室史，主录记书，催期会。

translations.literal: A master of records in charge of copying documents and urging deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: The master of records maintained correspondence and enforced meeting schedules.

sentences.zh: 无令史。

translations.literal: There were no order-clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The post of order-clerk was omitted.

sentences.zh: 阁下及诸曹各有书佐，干主文书。

translations.literal: Below the pavilion gate and in each bureau there were document assistants who managed paperwork.
translations.idiomatic: Under the gate and in every bureau document assistants handled the written work.

sentences.zh: 漢官曰：「河南尹員吏九百二十七人，十二人百石。

translations.literal: Han Offices says: "The Intendant of Henan had nine hundred twenty-seven clerks on the establishment, twelve at one hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Offices lists: "The Intendant of Henan with nine hundred twenty-seven clerks, twelve at one hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 諸縣有秩三十五人，官屬掾史五人，四部督郵〔吏〕部掾二十六人，案獄仁恕三人，監津渠漕水掾二十五人，百石卒吏二百五十人，文學守助掾六十人，書佐五十人，〔脩〕行二百三十人，幹小史二百三十一人。」

translations.literal: Ranked officers in the counties thirty-five; bureau clerks five; twenty-six route-inspector section clerks for four divisions; three humane case-review clerks; twenty-five canal and transport water clerks; two hundred fifty hundred-picul runner clerks; sixty literary aide clerks; fifty document assistants; [xiu] runners two hundred thirty; document runners two hundred thirty-one."
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-five county ranked officers; five bureau clerks; twenty-six route-inspector section clerks; three humane case reviewers; twenty-five canal clerks; two hundred fifty runner clerks; sixty literary aides; fifty document assistants; two hundred thirty runners; and two hundred thirty-one document runners."

sentences.zh: 属官，每县、邑、道，大者置令一人，千石：其次置长，四百石；

translations.literal: Subordinate offices: for each county, town, or circuit, the largest had one magistrate at one thousand piculs;
translations.idiomatic: Below them, each county, noble town, or barbarian circuit of the first rank had a magistrate at one thousand piculs;

sentences.zh: 小者置长，三百石；

translations.literal: the next size had a chief at four hundred piculs;
translations.idiomatic: middle-sized units had a chief at four hundred piculs;

sentences.zh: 侯国之相，秩次亦如之。

translations.literal: the chancellors of marquisates followed the same salary ladder.
translations.idiomatic: chancellors of marquisates were paid on the same stepped scale.

sentences.zh: 應劭漢官曰：「前書百官表云，萬戸以上爲令，萬戸以下爲長。

translations.literal: Ying Shao's Han Offices says: "The Former Book's table of offices states that ten thousand households or more made a magistrate, below ten thousand made a chief.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Han Offices cites the Former Book: "Ten thousand households or more made a magistrate; fewer made a chief.

sentences.zh: 三邊始孝武皇帝所開，縣戸數百而或爲令。

translations.literal: The three frontiers were first opened by Emperor Wu; counties with only several hundred households might still have a magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: On the three frontiers opened by Emperor Wu, counties of only a few hundred households might still rate a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 荊揚江南七郡，唯有臨湘、南昌、呉三令爾。

translations.literal: Among the seven commanderies of Jiangnan in Jing and Yang, only Linxiang, Nanchang, and Wu had magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Of the seven Jiangnan commanderies in Jing and Yang, only Linxiang, Nanchang, and Wu had magistrates.

sentences.zh: 及南陽穰中，土沃民稠，四五萬戸而爲長。

translations.literal: At Xiang in Nanyang the soil was fertile and the people dense—forty or fifty thousand households yet only a chief.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiang in Nanyang, fertile and crowded with forty or fifty thousand households, the post remained only a chief.

sentences.zh: 桓帝時，以〔汝〕南陽安爲女公主邑，改號爲令，主薨復復其故。

translations.literal: In Emperor Huan's time, because Nanyang An was a princess's fief, the title was changed to magistrate; when the princess died it reverted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huan, Nanyang An became a princess's fief and was promoted to magistrate; after her death the old title returned.

sentences.zh: 若此爲繫其本。

translations.literal: Cases like this tie back to the root principle.
translations.idiomatic: Such cases follow the underlying rule.

sentences.zh: 俗説令長以水土爲之，及秩髙下，皆無明文。

translations.literal: Popular explanation says magistrates and chiefs were made according to soil and water, and high or low rank had no written rule.
translations.idiomatic: Folk explanation ties magistrate and chief grades to local conditions, with no fixed written rule for rank.

sentences.zh: 班固通儒，述一代之書，斯近其眞。」

translations.literal: Ban Gu, a comprehensive scholar, described the institutions of an age—this comes near the truth."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu, master of the tradition, described an entire dynasty—this is closest to the truth."

sentences.zh: 本注曰：皆掌治民，显善劝义，禁奸罚恶，理讼平贼，恤民时务，秋冬集课，上计于所属郡国。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: All governed the people, displayed good and urged right conduct, forbade evil and punished wickedness, settled lawsuits and suppressed banditry, cared for the people’s seasonal tasks, gathered assessments in autumn and winter, and sent annual accounts up to the supervising commandery or kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: These officials governed the people, honored virtue, curbed vice, heard cases, kept the peace, timed corvée and taxes to the seasons, held autumn and winter reviews, and forwarded accounts to the parent commandery or kingdom.

sentences.zh: 胡廣曰：「秋冬歳盡，各計縣戸口墾田，錢穀入出，盜賊多少，上其集簿。

translations.literal: Hu Guang says: "At year's end in autumn and winter, each county tallied registered households, reclaimed fields, cash and grain in and out, and number of bandits, and submitted the summary register.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang explains: "At autumn and winter year's end each county reported households, reclaimed land, revenue, and banditry in summary registers.

sentences.zh: 丞尉以下，歳詣郡，課校其功。

translations.literal: Assistants and commandants and below went yearly to the commandery to have their merit examined and checked.
translations.idiomatic: Assistants and commandants went up yearly for performance review.

sentences.zh: 功多尤爲最者，於廷尉勞勉之，以勸其後。

translations.literal: Those with much merit and especially rated best were encouraged by the minister of justice to urge those who followed.
translations.idiomatic: Top performers were commended by the minister of justice to encourage the rest.

sentences.zh: 負多尤爲殿者，於後曹別責，以糾怠慢也。

translations.literal: Those with many faults and especially rated worst were separately reprimanded in the rear bureau to correct negligence.
translations.idiomatic: Worst performers were reprimanded in the rear bureau to correct slackness.

sentences.zh: 諸對辭窮尤困，收主者，掾史關白太守，使取法。

translations.literal: When replies were exhausted and especially distressed, the responsible party was taken; clerks reported to the grand administrator to apply the law.
translations.idiomatic: When suspects were cornered in interrogation, responsible parties were seized and clerks reported to the grand administrator for legal action.

sentences.zh: 丞尉縛責，以明下轉相督敕，爲民除害也。

translations.literal: Assistants and commandants bound and punished them, making clear that subordinates in turn supervised and admonished one another to remove harm for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Assistants and commandants bound and punished offenders, showing how each level supervised the next to protect the people.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔書不得僇辱黃綬，以別小人吏也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's edict forbade humiliating holders of the yellow ribbon, to distinguish petty clerks."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming forbade humiliating yellow-ribbon officers to separate petty clerks from higher ranks."

sentences.zh: 凡县主蛮夷曰道。

translations.literal: In general counties that chiefly held barbarians were called circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Counties whose population was chiefly non-Chinese were termed circuits.

sentences.zh: 公主所食汤沐曰邑。

translations.literal: Bathing towns granted to princesses were called towns.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue manors bestowed on princesses were called noble towns.

sentences.zh: 县万户以上为令，不满为长。

translations.literal: Counties of ten thousand households or more had magistrates; those below had chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Units with ten thousand households or more rated a magistrate; smaller ones had a chief.

sentences.zh: 侯国为相。

translations.literal: Marquisates had chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Marquisates were administered by chancellors.

sentences.zh: 皆秦制也。

translations.literal: All were Qin institutions.
translations.idiomatic: These arrangements descended from Qin practice.

sentences.zh: 丞各一人。

translations.literal: Each had one assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Each county-level unit had one assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 尉大县二人，小县一人。

translations.literal: Large counties had two commandants, small counties one.
translations.idiomatic: Populous counties fielded two police commandants; smaller ones had one.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：丞署文書。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The assistant managed documents.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The assistant supervised paperwork.

sentences.zh: 典知倉獄。

translations.literal: He was in charge of granaries and prisons.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw granaries and jails.

sentences.zh: 尉主盗贼。

translations.literal: The commandant was in charge of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant handled theft and robbery.

sentences.zh: 凡有賊發，主名不立，則推索行尋，案察奸宄，以起端緒。

translations.literal: Whenever a crime occurred and the culprit’s identity was unknown, he pursued leads, investigated hidden evil, and opened the trail.
translations.idiomatic: When a crime lacked a named perpetrator, he followed clues, rooted out accomplices, and opened the investigation.

sentences.zh: 應劭漢官曰：「大縣丞左右尉，所謂命卿三人。

translations.literal: Ying Shao's Han Offices says: "In large counties the assistant and left and right commandants—the so-called three life-peers.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Han Offices says: "A large county had an assistant and left and right commandants—the three so-called life-peers.

sentences.zh: 小縣一尉一丞，命卿二人。」

translations.literal: In small counties one commandant and one assistant—two life-peers."
translations.idiomatic: A small county had one commandant and one assistant—two life-peers."

sentences.zh: 各署诸曹掾史。

translations.literal: Each established various bureau clerks and secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Each county likewise staffed bureau clerks and secretaries.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：诸曹略如郡员，五官为廷掾，监乡五部，春夏为劝农掾，秋冬为制度掾。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The bureaus were roughly like those of a commandery; the steward of the five bureaus was the court clerk, supervising five rural districts; in spring and summer he was the clerk for encouraging agriculture, in autumn and winter the clerk for statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: County bureaus echoed commandery models; the steward of the five bureaus doubled as court clerk over five rural circuits, shifting in warm months to agricultural promotion and in cold months to legal compliance.

sentences.zh: 漢官曰：「雒陽令秩千石，丞三人四百石，孝廉左尉四百石，孝廉右尉四百石。

translations.literal: Han Offices says: "The Luoyang magistrate ranked at one thousand piculs; three assistants at four hundred piculs; filial-and-incorrupt left commandant at four hundred piculs; filial-and-incorrupt right commandant at four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Offices lists: "The Luoyang magistrate at one thousand piculs, three assistants at four hundred, and filial-and-incorrupt left and right commandants at four hundred each.

sentences.zh: 員吏七百九十六人，十三人四百石。

translations.literal: The establishment was seven hundred ninety-six clerks, thirteen at four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The staff totaled seven hundred ninety-six clerks, thirteen at four hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 鄕有秩、獄史五十六人，佐史、鄕佐七十七人，斗食、令史、嗇夫、假五十人，官掾史、幹小史二百五十人，書佐九十人，〔脩〕行二百六十人。」

translations.literal: Township ranked officers and prison clerks fifty-six; assistant clerks and township assistants seventy-seven; dou-food, order-clerks, requisition officers, and acting clerks fifty; bureau clerks and document runners two hundred fifty; document assistants ninety; [xiu] runners two hundred sixty."
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-six township ranked officers and prison clerks; seventy-seven assistant clerks and township aides; fifty dou-food, order-clerks, requisition officers, and acting clerks; two hundred fifty bureau clerks and document runners; ninety document assistants; and two hundred sixty runners."

sentences.zh: 乡置有秩、三老、游徼。

translations.literal: In each township there were salaried elders, three elders, and patrol officers.
translations.idiomatic: Each township appointed a salaried headman, three moral elders, and roving patrol officers.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：有秩，郡所署，秩百石，漢官曰：「鄕戸五千，則置有秩。」

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The ranked officer was appointed by the commandery at the one-hundred-picul grade. Han Offices says: "When a township had five thousand households, a ranked officer was placed."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The ranked officer was a commandery appointment at one hundred piculs. Han Offices adds: "Townships of five thousand households received a ranked officer."

sentences.zh: 掌一鄕人；

translations.literal: He governed one township's people;
translations.idiomatic: He governed the people of one township;

sentences.zh: 風俗通曰：「秩則田閒大夫，言其官裁有秩耳。」

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs says: "Ranked officer means field-side grandee—speaking of an office with measured authority."
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs explains: "Ranked officer means a field-side grandee—an office of measured authority."

sentences.zh: 其鄕小者，縣置嗇夫一人風俗通曰：「嗇者，省也。

translations.literal: Where the township was small, the county placed one requisition officer. The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs says: "Se means to examine.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller townships got one county requisition officer. The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs says: "Se means to examine.

sentences.zh: 夫，賦也。

translations.literal: Fu means levy.
translations.idiomatic: Fu means levy.

sentences.zh: 言消息百姓，均其役賦。」

translations.literal: It means to inform the people and equalize their corvée and levies."
translations.idiomatic: The title means to keep the people informed and balance corvée and levies."

sentences.zh: 皆主知民善恶，为役先后，知民贫富，为赋多少，平其差品。

translations.literal: All were to know the people’s good and evil, the order of labor service, the people’s wealth and poverty, and the amount of tax, and to equalize grades of assessment.
translations.idiomatic: They were to know who was virtuous or vicious, who should serve corvée first or last, who was rich or poor, how much tax each owed, and to keep assessments fair.

sentences.zh: 三老掌教化。

translations.literal: The three elders were in charge of moral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The three elders led moral education.

sentences.zh: 凡有孝子顺孙，贞女义妇，让财救患，及学士为民法式者，皆扁表其门，以兴善行。

translations.literal: Whenever there were filial sons, obedient grandsons, chaste wives, righteous women, those who yielded property or saved others in distress, and scholars who could model conduct for the people, their gates were inscribed to encourage good deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Filial children, chaste widows, donors, rescuers, and scholars who set an example had commendatory plaques hung on their gates to inspire the community.

sentences.zh: 遊徼掌徼循，禁司奸盜。

translations.literal: Patrol officers were in charge of patrols and prohibiting spying, theft, and robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol officers patrolled the countryside and suppressed spies, thieves, and robbers.

sentences.zh: 又有鄕佐，屬鄕，主民收賦稅風俗通曰：「國家制度，大率十里一鄕。」

translations.literal: There were also township assistants, subordinate to the township, in charge of collecting the people's taxes and levies. The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs says: "In the state's system, broadly every ten li formed one township.
translations.idiomatic: There were also township assistants under each township who collected taxes and levies. The Comprehensive Meaning of Customs says: "By state rule, roughly every ten li made one township."

sentences.zh: 亭有亭长，以禁盗贼。

translations.literal: Each ward post had a ward head to prohibit bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Every roadside ward had a ward head whose duty was to suppress banditry.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：亭长，主求捕盗贼，承望都尉。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The ward head was in charge of seeking and capturing bandits and answering to the commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Ward heads tracked down thieves and reported to the county commandant.

sentences.zh: 里有里魁，民有什伍，善恶以告。

translations.literal: In each hamlet there was a hamlet chief; the people were grouped in tens and fives, and good and evil were reported.
translations.idiomatic: Each hamlet had a chief; households were grouped in tens and fives so that conduct could be reported upward.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：里魁掌一里百家。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The hamlet chief governed one hamlet of a hundred families.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: A hamlet chief oversaw roughly one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 什主十家，伍主五家，以相检察。

translations.literal: The ten-chief governed ten families, the five-chief five families, mutually inspecting one another.
translations.idiomatic: Leaders of ten and five households watched one another in a mutual-surveillance grid.

sentences.zh: 民有善事恶事，以告监官。

translations.literal: When the people had good or evil deeds, they reported them to the supervising official.
translations.idiomatic: Good or bad behavior was relayed to the supervising magistrate.

sentences.zh: 边县有障塞尉。

translations.literal: Border counties had barrier-and-pass commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier counties posted commandants for barriers and passes.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌禁备羌夷犯塞。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: They were in charge of prohibitions and readiness against Qiang and Yi raiding the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: They guarded against Qiang and Yi incursions through the frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 太公陰符曰：「武王問太公：『願聞治亂之要。』

translations.literal: Taigong's Secret Tallies says: "King Wu asked Taigong: 'I wish to hear the essentials of order and disorder.'"
translations.idiomatic: Taigong's Secret Tallies records: "King Wu asked Taigong: 'I wish to hear the essentials of order and disorder.'"

sentences.zh: 太公曰：『其本在吏。』

translations.literal: Taigong said: 'Its root lies in officials.'
translations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'Its root lies in officials.'

sentences.zh: 武王曰：『吏者治也，所以爲治，其亂者何？』

translations.literal: King Wu said: 'Official means governance; they are what bring order—what brings disorder?'
translations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'Official means governance; they bring order—what brings disorder?'

sentences.zh: 太公曰：『故吏重罪有十。』

translations.literal: Taigong said: 'Therefore officials have ten heavy crimes.'
translations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'Therefore officials have ten heavy crimes.'

sentences.zh: 武王問『吏之重罪。』

translations.literal: King Wu asked about 'the officials' heavy crimes.'
translations.idiomatic: King Wu asked about 'the officials' heavy crimes.'

sentences.zh: 太公曰；

translations.literal: Taigong said;
translations.idiomatic: Taigong said;

sentences.zh: 『一、吏苛刻；

translations.literal: 'First, officials are harsh and severe;
translations.idiomatic: 'First, officials are harsh and severe;

sentences.zh: 二、吏不平；

translations.literal: second, officials are unfair;
translations.idiomatic: second, officials are unfair;

sentences.zh: 三、吏貪汚；

translations.literal: third, officials are greedy and corrupt;
translations.idiomatic: third, officials are greedy and corrupt;

sentences.zh: 四、吏以威力迫脅於民；

translations.literal: fourth, officials use power and might to coerce the people;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, officials use power to coerce the people;

sentences.zh: 五、吏與史合姦；

translations.literal: fifth, officials conspire with clerks;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, officials conspire with clerks;

sentences.zh: 六、吏與人亡情；

translations.literal: sixth, officials are heartless toward people;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, officials are heartless toward people;

sentences.zh: 七、吏作盜賊，使人爲耳目；

translations.literal: seventh, officials act as bandits and make men their eyes and ears;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, officials act as bandits and use men as spies;

sentences.zh: 八、吏賤買賣貴於民；

translations.literal: eighth, officials buy cheap and sell dear to the people;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, officials buy cheap and sell dear to the people;

sentences.zh: 九、吏增易於民；

translations.literal: ninth, officials alter and change accounts against the people;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, officials falsify accounts against the people;

sentences.zh: 十、吏振懼於民。

translations.literal: tenth, officials terrify the people.
translations.idiomatic: tenth, officials terrify the people.

sentences.zh: 夫治者有三罪，則國亂而民愁；

translations.literal: When rulers have three crimes, the state is disordered and the people grieved;
translations.idiomatic: When rulers commit three crimes, the state is disordered and the people grieved;

sentences.zh: 盡有之，則民流亡而君失其國。』

translations.literal: when they have all of them, the people flee and the ruler loses his state.'
translations.idiomatic: when they have all of them, the people flee and the ruler loses his state.'

sentences.zh: 武王曰：『民亦有罪乎？』

translations.literal: King Wu said: 'Do the people also have crimes?'
translations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'Do the people also have crimes?'

sentences.zh: 太公曰：『民有十大於此，除者則國治而民安。』

translations.literal: Taigong said: 'The people have ten greater than these; remove them and the state is governed and the people secure.'
translations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'The people have ten greater than these; remove them and the state is governed and the people secure.'

sentences.zh: 武王曰：『十大何如？』

translations.literal: King Wu said: 'What are the ten great ones like?'
translations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'What are the ten great ones?'

sentences.zh: 太公曰：『民勝吏，厚大臣，一大也。

translations.literal: Taigong said: 'The people overcome officials and enrich great ministers—one great crime.
translations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'The people overcome officials and enrich great ministers—the first great crime.

sentences.zh: 民宗強，侵陵群下，二大也。

translations.literal: The people honor the strong and encroach upon subordinates—two great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The people honor the strong and encroach upon subordinates—the second.

sentences.zh: 民甚富，傾國家，三大也。

translations.literal: The people are very rich and overturn the state—three great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The people grow very rich and overturn the state—the third.

sentences.zh: 民尊親其君，天下歸慕，四大也。

translations.literal: The people honor and cherish their lord and all under Heaven turns in admiration—four great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The people honor their lord and all under Heaven turns in admiration—the fourth.

sentences.zh: 衆暴寡，五大也。

translations.literal: The many oppress the few—five great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The many oppress the few—the fifth.

sentences.zh: 民有百里之譽，千里之交，六大也。

translations.literal: The people have fame for a hundred li and alliances for a thousand li—six great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The people win fame for a hundred li and alliances for a thousand li—the sixth.

sentences.zh: 民以吏威爲權，七大也。

translations.literal: The people take officials' authority as power—seven great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The people treat officials' authority as power—the seventh.

sentences.zh: 恩行於吏，八大也。

translations.literal: Favor flows through officials—eight great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Favor flows through officials—the eighth.

sentences.zh: 民服信，以少爲多，奪人田宅，贅人妻於，九大也。

translations.literal: The people are compliant and trusting, making few into many, seizing others' fields and dwellings, and taking others' wives in marriage—nine great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The people are compliant, inflate numbers, seize fields and dwellings, and take others' wives—the ninth.

sentences.zh: 民之基業畜産爲人所苦，十大也。

translations.literal: The people's foundations, estates, and livestock are harmed by others—ten great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The people's foundations, estates, and livestock are harmed by others—the tenth.

sentences.zh: 所謂一家害一里，一里害諸侯，諸侯害天下。』

translations.literal: This is what is called one household harming one ward, one ward harming feudal lords, feudal lords harming all under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called one household harming one ward, one ward harming feudal lords, feudal lords harming all under Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 武王曰：『絶吏之罪，塞民之大，奈何？』

translations.literal: King Wu said: 'How can one cut off officials' crimes and block the people's great crimes?'
translations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'How can one cut off officials' crimes and block the people's great crimes?'

sentences.zh: 太公曰：『察民之暴吏，明其賞，審其誅，則吏不敢犯罪，民不敢大也。』

translations.literal: Taigong said: 'Investigate violent officials among the people, clarify rewards, examine punishments, and officials will not dare to commit crimes and the people will not dare their great crimes.'
translations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'Investigate violent officials, clarify rewards, examine punishments, and officials will not dare crime nor the people their great crimes.'

sentences.zh: 武王曰：『是民吏相伺，上下不和而結其讎。』

translations.literal: King Wu said: 'This means people and officials spy on each other, above and below are not harmonious, and they form grudges.'
translations.idiomatic: King Wu said: 'Then people and officials spy on each other, above and below fall out, and grudges form.'

sentences.zh: 太公曰：『爲君守成，爲吏守職，爲民守事。

translations.literal: Taigong said: 'Let the ruler guard accomplishment, let officials guard their duties, let the people guard their tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Taigong said: 'Let the ruler guard accomplishment, officials guard their duties, and the people guard their tasks.

sentences.zh: 如此，各居其道則國治，國治則都治，都治則里治，里治則家治，家治則善惡分明，善惡分明則國無事，國無事則吏民外不懷怨，内不徼事。』」

translations.literal: Thus, each keeping to his path, the state is governed; when the state is governed the metropolis is governed; when the metropolis is governed the ward is governed; when the ward is governed the household is governed; when the household is governed good and evil are distinguished; when good and evil are distinguished the state has no affairs; when the state has no affairs officials and people outwardly harbor no resentment and inwardly seek no improper gain.'"
translations.idiomatic: Thus each keeps to his path: the state is governed, then the metropolis, ward, and household; good and evil are distinguished, the state has no affairs, and officials and people harbor no outward resentment or inward scheming.'"

sentences.zh: 其郡有盐官、铁官、工官、都水官者，随事广狭置令、长及丞，秩次皆如县、道，无分士，给均本吏。

translations.literal: In commanderies that had salt offices, iron offices, craft offices, or capital-construction water offices, according to the size of the task they placed magistrates, chiefs, and assistants; the salary grades were all like counties and circuits; there was no separate territorial jurisdiction; clerks were supplied evenly from the regular establishment.
