translations.idiomatic: Commanderies rich in salt, iron, crafts, or waterworks set magistrates, chiefs, and assistants scaled to the workload, paid like county officials, without an independent territory, drawing clerks from the standard pool.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：凡郡县出盐多者置盐官，主盐税。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In general commanderies and counties that produced much salt set salt offices in charge of salt tax.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Salty regions established salt bureaus to levy salt duties.

sentences.zh: 出鐵多者置鐵官，主鼓鑄。

translations.literal: Those that produced much iron set iron offices in charge of smelting and casting.
translations.idiomatic: Iron-rich areas placed iron bureaus to oversee smelting and minting.

sentences.zh: 胡廣曰：「鹽官掊坑而得鹽，或有鑿井煮海水而以得之者。

translations.literal: Hu Guang says: "Salt offices dug pits to obtain salt, or sometimes bored wells and boiled seawater to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang says: "Salt offices dug pits for salt, or bored wells and boiled seawater to obtain it.

sentences.zh: 鑄銅爲器械，當鑄冶之時，扇熾其火，謂之鼓鑄。」

translations.literal: Casting copper into implements, when smelting and forging, they fanned and stoked the fire—this was called drum-casting."
translations.idiomatic: Casting copper implements, they fanned and stoked the forge fire—called drum-casting."

sentences.zh: 有工多者置工官，主工税物。

translations.literal: Those with much craftwork set craft offices in charge of craft taxes and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Industrial centers added craft bureaus to tax manufactures.

sentences.zh: 有水池及鱼利多者置水官，主平水收渔税。

translations.literal: Those with ponds and much fish profit set water offices in charge of leveling water and collecting fishing tax.
translations.idiomatic: Where ponds and fisheries flourished, water bureaus regulated irrigation works and fishing levies.

sentences.zh: 在所诸县均差吏更给之。

translations.literal: In the relevant counties clerks were rotated in assignment to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk labor was rotated among nearby counties to staff these offices.

sentences.zh: 置吏随事，不具县员。

translations.literal: Clerks were placed according to the task and were not counted in the county’s regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: Such posts were ad hoc and did not count toward the county’s authorized headcount.

sentences.zh: 使匈奴中郎将一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One Herald to the Xiongnu, comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: A single Herald to the Xiongnu held rank comparable to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主护南单于。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of protecting the Southern Shanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He guarded the interests of the Southern Shanyu’s court.

sentences.zh: 置从事二人，有事随事增之，掾随事为员。

translations.literal: Two attendants were established; when there was business they were increased according to the matter; clerks were appointed as needed for the task.
translations.idiomatic: Two staff attendants were standard; extra aides and clerks were added when duties required.

sentences.zh: 护羌、乌桓校尉所置亦然。

translations.literal: The establishment of the Protectors of the Qiang and Wuhuan was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Protectors of the Qiang and Wuhuan were organized on the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 护乌桓校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One Protector of the Wuhuan, comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: One Protector of the Wuhuan held rank comparable to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主乌桓胡。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of the Wuhuan Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He supervised the Wuhuan tribes on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 护羌校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One Protector of the Qiang, comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: One Protector of the Qiang held rank comparable to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主西羌。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of the Western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: His brief covered the western Qiang peoples.

sentences.zh: 皇子封王，其郡为国，每置傅一人，相一人，皆二千石。

translations.literal: When imperial sons were enfeoffed as kings, their commanderies became kingdoms; each had one tutor and one chancellor, both at two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes received kingdoms built on commanderies, each staffed with a tutor and a chancellor at two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：傅主导王以善，礼如师，不臣也。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The tutor guided the king toward goodness with ritual like a teacher and was not treated as a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The tutor instructed the prince in virtue with the deference due a teacher rather than a minister.

sentences.zh: 相如太守。

translations.literal: The chancellor was like a grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom chancellor corresponded to a commandery grand administrator.

sentences.zh: 其长史，如郡丞。

translations.literal: Its chief clerk was like a commandery assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom chief clerk matched a commandery assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 汉初立诸王，因项羽所立诸王之制，地既广大，且至千里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Han, when the various kings were established, they followed the system of kings set up by Xiang Yu; the territory was vast, reaching as much as a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han princes inherited Xiang Yu’s sprawling kingdoms, some stretching a thousand li across.

sentences.zh: 又其官职，傅为太傅，相为丞相，又有御史大夫及诸卿，皆秩二千石，百官皆如朝廷。

translations.literal: Moreover their offices: the tutor was grand tutor, the chancellor was chancellor of state, and there were also imperial clerks and the various ministers, all at two thousand piculs, the hundred officials all like the court.
translations.idiomatic: Their governments copied the capital: grand tutor, chancellor of state, censor-in-chief, and ministers at two thousand piculs—a full court in miniature.

sentences.zh: 国家唯为置丞相，其御史大夫以下皆自置之。

translations.literal: The state only set up the chancellor for them; from the censor-in-chief downward they appointed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The central government named only the chancellor; princes chose their own censor-in-chief and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 至景帝时，吴、楚七国恃其国大，遂以作乱，几危汉室。

translations.literal: By Emperor Jing’s time, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu relied on their great size and then rebelled, nearly endangering the Han house.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jing the great kingdoms of Wu and Chu rose in revolt and nearly toppled the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及其诛灭，景帝惩之，遂令诸王不得治民，令内史主治民，改丞相曰相，省御史大夫、廷尉、少府、宗正、博士官。

translations.literal: When they were exterminated, Emperor Jing took warning and ordered the kings not to govern the people, ordered interior clerks to govern the people instead, changed the chancellor of state to chancellor, and abolished the posts of censor-in-chief, commandant of justice, privy treasurer, director of the imperial clan, and erudits.
translations.idiomatic: After their defeat Emperor Jing stripped princes of civil authority, transferred rule to imperial clerks, downgraded the chief minister to “chancellor,” and eliminated replica ministries such as justice, finance, clan affairs, and the academy.

sentences.zh: 武帝改漢内史、中尉、郎中令之名，前書曰：「改漢内史爲京兆尹，中尉爲執金吾，郎中令爲光祿勳。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu changed the Han names of interior clerk, commandant of the capital, and chamberlain for the palace guard. The Former Book says: "He changed Han interior clerk to metropolitan intendant of Jingzhao, commandant of the capital to commander of the metropolitan guard, and chamberlain for the palace guard to superintendent of the imperial clan."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu renamed the kingdom interior clerk, capital commandant, and chamberlain for the guard. The Former Book records: "The Han interior clerk became metropolitan intendant of Jingzhao, the capital commandant became commander of the metropolitan guard, and the chamberlain for the palace guard became superintendent of the imperial clan."

sentences.zh: 而王國如故，員職皆朝廷爲署，不得自置。

translations.literal: But the kingdoms remained as before; all posts were appointed by the court and could not be self-appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet kingdom appointments for every office now came from the center, not the prince.

sentences.zh: 至成帝省内史治民，更令相治民，漢舊儀曰：「大司空何武奏罷内史，相如太守，中尉如都尉，參職。

translations.literal: By Emperor Cheng the interior clerk who governed the people was abolished and the chancellor was ordered to govern the people instead. Han Old Observances says: "Grand Minister of Works He Wu memorialized to abolish the interior clerk; the chancellor was like a grand administrator, the commandant of the capital like a commandant, sharing duties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng abolished the kingdom interior clerk and transferred civil government to the chancellor. Han Old Observances records: "Grand Minister of Works He Wu memorialized to abolish the interior clerk; the chancellor was like a grand administrator and the capital commandant like a commandery commandant, sharing duties.

sentences.zh: 是後中尉爭權，與王相奏，常不和也。」

translations.literal: After this the commandant of the capital struggled for power with the king's chancellor and they often submitted accusations against each other and were constantly at odds."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the capital commandant and the king's chancellor struggled for power and constantly accused one another."

sentences.zh: 太傅但曰傅。

translations.literal: The grand tutor was simply called tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The grand tutor was shortened to "tutor."

sentences.zh: 臣昭曰：觀夫髙祖之創業也，豈直鴻勳碩德，大庇群生，蕩其毒虐，厝之和泰而已哉！

translations.literal: Chen Zhao says: Observing Gaozu's founding enterprise, was it only great merit and vast virtue, greatly sheltering the living masses, sweeping away cruelty and tyranny, and placing them in harmony and peace?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhao writes: Was Gaozu's founding only a matter of great merit, sheltering the people, and restoring peace?

sentences.zh: 至於謀深慮久，封建子弟，蕃維盤固，規謀弘遠。

translations.literal: As to deep planning and long forethought, enfeoffing sons and younger brothers, making the screen of defense firm and secure—the design was vast and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: His deep planning enfeoffed sons and younger brothers to make the defensive screen firm—a design vast and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 及於三趙不終，燕靈夭絶，齊、代、淮、楚皆爲外重，故宋昌曰「外畏齊、楚、淮南」，斯非效與？

translations.literal: When the three Zhao lines did not endure, Yan and Ling perished young, and Qi, Dai, Huai, and Chu all became heavy external powers, therefore Song Chang said "outwardly fearing Qi, Chu, and Huainan"—was this not effective?
translations.idiomatic: When the three Zhao lines failed, Yan and Ling died young, and Qi, Dai, Huai, and Chu became powerful external domains, Song Chang said "outwardly fearing Qi, Chu, and Huainan"—was that not proof?

sentences.zh: 事過則獘，孰或通之？

translations.literal: When affairs pass their limit, decay follows—who can fully penetrate this?
translations.idiomatic: When affairs pass their limit, decay follows—who does not see it?

sentences.zh: 全國之難，誠固財物之富，作衞之益，亦旣得之於前矣，故賜以幾杖，用息姦謀。

translations.literal: The difficulty of preserving a whole state truly lay in the wealth of goods and the benefit of forming guards—this had already been gained before; therefore they were granted cane and staff to quiet treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Preserving a whole state required wealth and guards; hence canes and staffs were granted to quiet treacherous designs.

sentences.zh: 嗣隕局下，怨生有以，逮連師構亂，兵交梁闕，禦侮摧寇，肇自密戚。

translations.literal: When heirs fell in the lower ranks, resentment had its cause; when allied armies stirred rebellion and weapons clashed at the beams and towers of the palace, defense against insult and crushing of invaders began with close kin.
translations.idiomatic: When heirs fell and resentment grew, allied armies clashed at the palace gates—defense and rebellion alike began among close kin.

sentences.zh: 景帝遂削蕃國之權，刻骨肉之援，封爲君而不聽治其民，置爲主而稍賤其臣，矯枉過甚，遂臻於此。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing then cut the power of frontier kingdoms, carved to the bone the support of flesh and blood, enfeoffed men as lords but did not let them govern their people, made them masters but gradually debased their ministers—correcting the bend went too far and thus reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing then stripped frontier kingdoms of power, cut flesh-and-blood support, made princes lords without civil rule and masters with debased ministers—overcorrecting until this result.

sentences.zh: 呂、霍之危朝，后族愈貴於來寵，呉、楚之叛奔，侯王恆藉以受誚，故賈誼欲衆建以少其力，列虚以侯其生，此乃達觀深識，監於親陪之要者也。

translations.literal: The Lü and Huo crises endangered the court; empress clans grew ever more honored through favor; Wu and Chu rebelled and fled; marquises and kings constantly borrowed these to receive reproach; therefore Jia Yi wished to establish many fiefs to diminish their strength and set empty ranks to wait for their birth—this was penetrating vision and deep insight, watching the essentials of close kin and companions.
translations.idiomatic: The Lü and Huo crises, favored empress clans, and Wu-Chu rebellion brought constant reproach on princes; Jia Yi therefore wished to multiply fiefs to diminish their strength—a penetrating insight into kin politics.

sentences.zh: 冢嗣必傳萬裏之地，分支欲使動搖不得，於經維遠筭，且已礙矣。

translations.literal: The heir must transmit lands of ten thousand li; collateral branches were to be kept from stirring—yet in long-range planning this already obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: The heir must inherit vast lands while collateral lines were kept from stirring—already an obstacle to long-range planning.

sentences.zh: 復哀平之際，劉氏遍於四海，宗正著録，遂以萬數。

translations.literal: Again at the Ai and Ping period the Liu clan spread across the four seas; the director of the imperial clan's register counted them by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: By the Ai and Ping reigns the Liu clan spread across the realm and the imperial clan register counted them by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 及乎後漢，彌循前跡，光武十子，並列畿外近郡，孝明八國，不能開庇遠民。

translations.literal: By Later Han they followed the former track still more; Guangwu's ten sons were all placed in near commanderies outside the capital region; Ming's eight kingdoms could not open and shelter distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han followed the same path: Guangwu's ten sons held near domains outside the capital, and Ming's eight kingdoms could not shelter distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 國近則不可以大，不大則不足爲強，此所以本枝之援，終以少固。

translations.literal: Kingdoms near the center could not be large; if not large they were insufficient to be strong—therefore support from root and branches ultimately remained slight and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Near domains could not be large, and without size they could not be strong—so root-and-branch support remained slight.

sentences.zh: 若使漢分兩越置二三親國，剖呉、楚樹數四列蕃，割遼海而分皇枝，開隴蜀而王子弟，使主尊顯，依漢初之貴，民無定限，許滋養之富；

translations.literal: If Han had divided the two Yue regions and placed two or three close kin kingdoms, carved Wu and Chu and planted several rows of four frontier screens, cut Liaohai and divided royal branches, opened Long and Shu and enfeoffed sons and younger brothers, making lords honored and eminent according to early Han nobility, with no fixed limit on people and allowing nourishing wealth;
translations.idiomatic: If Han had divided the two Yue regions into close kin kingdoms, carved Wu and Chu into several frontier screens, split Liaohai and Long-Shu among royal branches, and allowed lords the early Han honor and unlimited people to nourish wealth;

sentences.zh: 若有昏虐之嗣，可得廢而不得削，必傳劉氏。

translations.literal: if there were brutal and tyrannical heirs, they could be deposed but not reduced, and the Liu line must be transmitted;
translations.idiomatic: if brutal heirs appeared they could be deposed but not reduced, and the Liu line would endure;

sentences.zh: 民信所奉，發其侵伐兼幷之釁，峻其他族篡殺之科，制其入貢輕重之法，疎其來朝往復之數。

translations.literal: the people would trust whom they served; signs of invasion, attack, and merger would be exposed; penalties for other clans' usurpation and murder would be severe; methods for regulating tribute weight would be set; and the number of visits to court would be spaced.
translations.idiomatic: the people would trust their lords; signs of aggression would be exposed; usurpation by other clans would be severely punished; tribute and court visits would be regulated;

sentences.zh: 君君臣臣，永許百世之期，一國之民，長無遷動之志，四方得志，聽離官列封，懷賢抱智，隨所適樂土。

translations.literal: lord and minister, lord and minister, would be granted a covenant for a hundred generations; the people of one state would long have no will to migrate; the four quarters achieving their aims would be allowed to leave office and receive enfeoffment; cherishing worth and embracing wisdom, each would go where pleased to a happy land.
translations.idiomatic: lord and minister would covenant for a hundred generations; a state's people would not migrate; the talented would go where they pleased;

sentences.zh: 強弱相侔，遠近相摧，舉其大歸，略其小滯，與其畫一，班之海内。

translations.literal: Strong and weak would balance one another, far and near would check one another; taking the great principle and omitting small hindrances, granting each its measure, this would be distributed within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: strong and weak would balance, far and near would check one another; taking the great principle and distributing it within the seas;

sentences.zh: 天子之朝，自非異姓僭奪，不得興勤王之師。

translations.literal: at the Son of Heaven's court, unless there were usurpation by another surname, no army to rescue the king could be raised.
translations.idiomatic: the court would raise no rescue army unless another surname usurped the throne;

sentences.zh: 諸蕃國，自非雜互篡主，不降討伐之詔。

translations.literal: among all frontier kingdoms, unless there were mixed usurpation of lords, no decree of punitive campaign would be issued.
translations.idiomatic: frontier kingdoms would receive no punitive decree unless lords usurped one another;

sentences.zh: 犬牙相經，共爲嚴國，雖王莽善盜，將何因而敢竊，曹操雄勇，亦安能以得士。

translations.literal: interlocking like dogs' teeth, together forming a stern realm—even if Wang Mang were skilled at theft, by what means could he dare to seize; even if Cao Cao were fierce and brave, how could he win men by force.
translations.idiomatic: interlocking like dogs' teeth into a stern realm—even Wang Mang could not steal the throne, nor Cao Cao win men by force.

sentences.zh: 斯無俟極聖然克行，明賢粗識亦足立。

translations.literal: This need not wait for the utmost sage to accomplish; a clear worthy with rough understanding would suffice to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: This need not wait for the utmost sage; a clear worthy with rough understanding could establish it.

sentences.zh: 故父子首足也，昆弟四支也，當使筋骨髓血，動靜足以相勝，長短大小，幹用足以相衞。

translations.literal: Therefore father and son are head and foot; elder and younger brothers are the four limbs; sinew, bone, marrow, and blood in movement and stillness should suffice to overcome one another; long and short, large and small, trunk and use should suffice to guard one another.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son are head and foot; brothers are the four limbs; sinew, bone, marrow, and blood should balance movement and stillness and guard one another.

sentences.zh: 豈有割脛致腹，取骨肉以增頭，剗背露骨，剝膏腴以裨頷，而謂顱顙魁岸，可得比壽松、晉，喉咽擁腫，必能長生久視哉？

translations.literal: How could one cut the shank to enlarge the belly, take flesh and bone to add to the head, scrape the back to expose bone, strip rich fat to pad the jaw, and then say the skull and brow are lofty and massive, comparable to the longevity of pine and Jin, or that a swollen throat and neck must assure long life and far sight?
translations.idiomatic: Who cuts the shank to enlarge the belly, strips the back to pad the jaw, and then claims a lofty brow like the pine of longevity or a swollen throat that assures long life?

sentences.zh: 漢氏得之微，猶能四百載，魏人失之甚，不滿數十年。

translations.literal: The Han house gained it slightly and still endured four hundred years; Wei men lost it greatly and did not last several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Han gained it slightly and endured four hundred years; Wei lost it greatly and did not last decades.

sentences.zh: 爰自晉世，矯枉太過，入列皇朝，非簡賢之授，唯親是貴，無愚智之辨。

translations.literal: From the Jin age onward, correcting the bend went too far; entering the ranks of the imperial clan was not appointment by selecting the worthy—only kin was honored, with no distinction between foolish and wise.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin onward overcorrection made imperial rank honor kin alone, with no distinction between foolish and wise.

sentences.zh: 不能勝衣冠，早據公相之尊，童蒙幼子，遄登槐嶽之位。

translations.literal: Unable to surpass ordinary officials in dress, they early occupied the honor of excellencies and chancellors; infant children swiftly ascended posts on the locust-and-catalpa terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to surpass ordinary officials, infant children swiftly occupied excellencies and chancellorships.

sentences.zh: 職應論道，而未離保母之養，續侯賦政，而服二三尺衣。

translations.literal: Their duties should have been to discourse on the Way, yet they had not left the nurse's care; continuing as marquises and administering government, they still wore clothes of two or three feet.
translations.idiomatic: They should discourse on the Way yet had not left the nurse's care; they governed yet still wore child's clothing.

sentences.zh: 英賢大度，稟彼昏稚，髙才碩儒，恭承藐識。

translations.literal: Heroic worthies of broad mind received instruction from those childish and young; men of high talent and great learning respectfully served their slight understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Heroic worthies received instruction from the childish; great scholars respectfully served slight understanding.

sentences.zh: 公餗覆而不憂，美錦碎而愈截。

translations.literal: The public cauldron was overturned without worry; fine brocade was shattered and cut still more.
translations.idiomatic: The public cauldron was overturned without worry; fine brocade was shattered and cut still more.

sentences.zh: 兼授若流，迴遷競路，才駑任重，功尠釁多。

translations.literal: Concurrent appointments flowed like a stream; roundabout transfers competed on the road; talent was dull yet burden heavy; achievement slight yet fault many.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent appointments flowed endlessly; talent was dull yet burdens heavy; achievement slight yet faults many.

sentences.zh: 曉比名於公旦，夕同罪於盜跖，褒稱無位，可以充德，貶退刑轘，不足以塞咎。

translations.literal: In the morning compared in name to the Duke of Zhou; by evening sharing guilt with Robber Zhi; praise without rank could fill virtue; demotion and execution by quartering could not suffice to cover fault.
translations.idiomatic: Praised in the morning as the Duke of Zhou and condemned by evening as Robber Zhi; praise without rank could not fill virtue, nor execution cover fault.

sentences.zh: 〔威〕力強濟，聲實隆重，嫌猜畏逼，身受其獘。

translations.literal: [Power] was forcibly propped up; reputation and substance were weighty; suspicion and fear pressed hard; they personally suffered decay.
translations.idiomatic: Power was forcibly propped up; reputation was weighty; suspicion pressed hard; they personally suffered ruin.

sentences.zh: 覆滅分體，若梟仇寇，〔齏〕粉同氣，有過他逆。

translations.literal: Overthrow and extinction split the body, like displaying a foe as an owl; [pulverizing] flesh of the same breath exceeded other rebellions.
translations.idiomatic: Overthrow split the body like displaying a foe; pulverizing kin exceeded other rebellions.

sentences.zh: 忠貞之士，橫羅其凶，志節之人，狼狽其禍。

translations.literal: Loyal and steadfast men were swept into their calamity; men of resolve and integrity were battered by their disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal men were swept into calamity; men of resolve were battered by disaster.

sentences.zh: 閼伯、實沈，繼踵史筆，顯思顯甫，比有國書。

translations.literal: Quebo and Shichen followed one after another in the historians' brush; Xian Si and Xian Fu were compared in state documents.
translations.idiomatic: Quebo and Shichen followed in the historians' brush; Xian Si and Xian Fu appeared in state documents.

sentences.zh: 趙倫以〔憃〕愚排天，齊攸以賢明謝世，枉鬱殄夷，冤孫就盡，不可勝載矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Lun with [foolish] stupidity overturned Heaven; Qi You with worthy clarity departed the world; wrongful oppression exterminated and destroyed; innocent descendants were exhausted—too many to record.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lun with foolish stupidity overturned Heaven; Qi You with worthy clarity departed the world; wrongful oppression destroyed innocent descendants beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 豈周、漢之君多孝悌之性，晉、宋之主稟豺狼之情，蓋事勢使之然也。

translations.literal: Were Zhou and Han rulers mostly endowed with filial and brotherly nature, while Jin and Song lords possessed wolfish feeling? It was circumstance that made it so.
translations.idiomatic: Were Zhou and Han rulers more filial while Jin and Song lords were wolfish? Circumstance made it so.

sentences.zh: 朝行斯術，夕窮崩亂，未能革悛，來事愈甚。

translations.literal: Practicing this method in the morning, by evening they reached collapse and disorder; unable to reform and repent, later affairs grew worse still.
translations.idiomatic: Practicing this in the morning, by evening came collapse; unable to reform, later affairs grew worse.

sentences.zh: 蒼生爲此將盡矣，四海爲此構蹙矣！

translations.literal: The living masses for this will nearly be exhausted; the four seas for this are wrung with distress!
translations.idiomatic: The living masses will nearly be exhausted; the four seas are wrung with distress!

sentences.zh: 聖帝英君，欲反斯敗，必當更開同姓之國，置不增之約，罷皇胤入宮之禍，守盟牲礪河之篤，乃可還嶮墜之路，反乎全安之轍也。

translations.literal: Sage emperors and heroic rulers wishing to reverse this failure must reopen kingdoms of the same surname, establish covenants not to enlarge them, abolish the disaster of imperial descendants entering the palace, keep the solemnity of covenant victims and sharpening the river, and only then can they return from the precipitous falling path and turn back to the track of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: Sage rulers wishing to reverse this failure must reopen same-surname kingdoms, covenant not to enlarge them, end the disaster of imperial descendants in the palace, and keep solemn covenants—only then can they return to complete security.

sentences.zh: 中尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One commandant of the capital for the kingdom, comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Each kingdom appointed one capital commandant at rank comparable to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：职如郡都尉，主盗贼。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The duties were like those of a commandery commandant; he was in charge of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: His portfolio matched a commandery commandant’s, with chief responsibility for theft and robbery.

sentences.zh: 東觀書曰：「其紹封削絀者，中尉、内史官屬亦以率減。」

translations.literal: The Eastern Lodge Documents say: "When enfeoffment was continued but the fief reduced, the commandant and inner secretary staffs were also reduced proportionally."
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Lodge Documents note: "When a continued enfeoffment was cut back, the commandant and inner secretary staffs were reduced in proportion."

sentences.zh: 郎中令一人，僕一人，皆千石。

translations.literal: One director of attendants and one steward, both at one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: One director of attendants and one steward, each at the one-thousand-picul grade.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：郎中令掌王大夫、郎中宿衞，官如光祿勛。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The director of attendants was in charge of the king's grandees and bodyguards on night duty; the office was like the director of the retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The director of attendants supervised the king's grandees and palace guards on night duty, ranking like the court's director of the retinue.

sentences.zh: 自省少府，职皆并焉。

translations.literal: From the privy treasurer downward all functions were merged into it.
translations.idiomatic: From the privy treasurer on down, those duties were folded into his office.

sentences.zh: 仆主车及驭，如太仆。

translations.literal: The steward was in charge of chariots and driving, like the grand coachman.
translations.idiomatic: The steward managed carriages and teams, paralleling the grand coachman at court.

sentences.zh: 本曰太仆，比二千石，武帝改，但曰仆，又皆减其秩。

translations.literal: Originally called grand coachman, comparable to two thousand piculs; Emperor Wu changed it to simply steward, and also reduced all their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The post had been the grand coachman at “comparable to two thousand piculs”; Emperor Wu shortened the title to steward and cut the salary grades across the board.

sentences.zh: 治书，比六百石。

translations.literal: Document clerks, comparable to six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom document clerks held rank comparable to six hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：治书本尚书更名。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: Document clerks were the former masters of writing of the palace secretary, renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: They were the old “masters of writing” staff of the imperial secretary, retitled for service in a princely household.

sentences.zh: 大夫，比六百石。

translations.literal: Grandees, comparable to six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Household grandees ranked at six hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：无员。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: No fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: There was no statutory headcount.

sentences.zh: 掌奉王使至京都，奉璧贺正月，及使诸国。

translations.literal: They bore the king’s missions to the capital, presented the jade disc to congratulate on the first month, and were dispatched to other states.
translations.idiomatic: They carried the prince’s embassies to the capital, presented the congratulatory jade token at New Year audiences, and traveled on mission to other kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 本皆持节，后去节。

translations.literal: Originally all carried staffs of authority; later the staff was removed.
translations.idiomatic: At first they carried credentialed staffs; later that emblem was dropped.

sentences.zh: 谒者，比四百石。

translations.literal: Ushers, comparable to four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Ushers were graded at four hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌冠长冠。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of the king’s formal cap and long court cap.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: They guarded the ritual regalia—the capping cap and the long court headdress—used when the king received investiture or held court.

sentences.zh: 本員十六人，後減。

translations.literal: Originally the establishment was sixteen men; later it was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The corps once numbered sixteen; later it was trimmed.

sentences.zh: 礼乐长。

translations.literal: Director of ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: A director of ritual and music headed the princely orchestra and ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主乐人。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He supervised the household musicians.

sentences.zh: 卫士长。

translations.literal: Captain of the guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: A captain of the guardsmen commanded the standing watch.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主卫士。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of the guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He led the palace guard contingent.

sentences.zh: 医工长。

translations.literal: Chief of physicians.
translations.idiomatic: A chief physician oversaw the medical staff.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主医药。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He managed drugs and treatment for the household.

sentences.zh: 永巷长。

translations.literal: Warden of the everlasting lane.
translations.idiomatic: A warden of the “everlasting lane” policed the inner quarters’ corridors.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：宦者，主宫中婢使。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: A eunuch; in charge of palace maids and serving women.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The post was held by a eunuch who directed maidservants in the harem wing.

sentences.zh: 祠祀长。

translations.literal: Director of sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: A director of sacrifices arranged the princely ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主祠祀。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He handled offerings at the princely shrines.

sentences.zh: 皆比四百石。

translations.literal: All were comparable to four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: These specialist heads all drew pay comparable to four hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 自禮樂長至此，皆四百石。

translations.literal: From the Director of Rites and Music to this office, all were at four hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: From the Director of Rites and Music to this office, all were at four hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 郎中，二百石。

translations.literal: Gentlemen attendants, two hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen of the household guard stood at two hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：无员。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: No fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: There was no statutory headcount.

sentences.zh: 卫公、宋公。

translations.literal: The Dukes of Wei and Song.
translations.idiomatic: The chapter next treats the Dukes of Wei and Song, fiefs honoring the ancient dynastic lines.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：建武二年，封周后姬常为周承休公；

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In the second year of Jianwu he enfeoffed Ji Chang, a descendant of the Zhou, as Duke Who Continues the Blessings of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In Jianwu 2 the emperor enfeoffed Ji Chang, heir of the Zhou royal house, as duke charged with continuing Zhou’s blessing;

sentences.zh: 五年，封殷后孔安为殷绍嘉公。

translations.literal: in the fifth year he enfeoffed Kong An, a descendant of Yin, as Duke Who Connects the Luster of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: in Jianwu 5 he enfeoffed Kong An, scion of the Yin (Shang) line, as duke tasked with linking Yin’s residual glory to the Han.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改常为卫公，安为宋公，以为汉宾，在三公上。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he changed Chang to Duke of Wei and An to Duke of Song, making them guest-lords of the Han, ranked above the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 13 Ji Chang became Duke of Wei and Kong An Duke of Song, honored as ritual “guests” of the Han and seated above the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 五經通義：「二王之後不考功，有誅無絶。」

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics says: "The descendants of the two former dynasties are not examined for merit; they may be punished but not extinguished."
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics holds: "Descendants of the two former dynasties are not graded for merit—they may be punished but never cut off."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄曰：「王者存二代而封及五，郊天用天子禮以祭其始祖，行其正朔，此謂通三統也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "The king preserves the two former dynasties and enfeoffs up to five; in suburban sacrifice to Heaven he uses the Son of Heaven's rites to sacrifice to his founding ancestor and observes their calendar—this is called penetrating the three successions.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: "The king preserves two former dynasties and enfeoffs as many as five; he sacrifices to Heaven with royal rites for their founding ancestors and keeps their calendars—this is penetrating the three successions.

sentences.zh: 三恪者，敬其先聖，封其後而已，無殊異者也。」

translations.literal: The three reverent lines merely honor their former sages and enfeoff their descendants—that is all; there is nothing extraordinary about them."
translations.idiomatic: The three reverent lines simply honor former sages and enfeoff their heirs—nothing more distinctive than that."

sentences.zh: 列侯，所食县为侯国。

translations.literal: Full marquises: the county from which they drew income became a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: A full marquis took his stipendiary county as his marquisate.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：承秦爵二十等，为彻侯，金印紫绶，以赏有功。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: Continuing the Qin system of twenty ranks, they were complete marquises with gold seal and purple ribbon, to reward merit.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The rank continued the Qin twentieth grade—the complete marquis—with gold seal and purple cord, as the highest reward for service.

sentences.zh: 功大者食县，小者食乡、亭，得臣其所食吏民。

translations.literal: Those of great merit fed from a whole county; the lesser fed from a township or ward, and were allowed to treat the clerks and people they fed from as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest meritorious lords drew an entire county; lesser ones drew only a township or a ward, and might treat the households within that endowment as personal dependents.

sentences.zh: 后避武帝讳，为列侯。

translations.literal: Later, to avoid Emperor Wu’s taboo, they were called full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Later the title was softened to “full marquis” to avoid the taboo on Emperor Wu’s personal name (from “complete” marquis).

sentences.zh: 武帝元朔二年，令诸王得推恩分众子土，国家为封，亦为列侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshuo, Emperor Wu allowed kings to "extend favor" by subdividing domains for younger sons; the court packaged those parcels as full marquisates.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanshuo, Emperor Wu allowed kings to "extend favor" by subdividing domains for younger sons; the court packaged those parcels as full marquisates.

sentences.zh: 旧列侯奉朝请在长安者，位次三公。

translations.literal: Formerly full marquises who attended court and awaited summons in Chang’an ranked just below the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, full marquises who maintained residences in Chang’an and answered periodic court summons stood immediately beneath the three excellencies in order of precedence.

sentences.zh: 中興以來，唯以功德賜位特進者，次車騎將軍；

translations.literal: Hu Guang's Han Institutions says: "Those of outstanding merit whom the court especially honors are granted specially advanced rank, below the three excellencies but not below the general of chariots and cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang's Han Institutions explains: "Peers of exceptional merit whom the court singles out receive specially advanced rank—below the three excellencies but not beneath the general of chariots and cavalry."

sentences.zh: 胡廣漢制度曰：「功德優盛，朝廷所敬異者，賜特進，在三公下，不在車騎下。」

translations.literal: Hu Guang's Han Institutions says: "Those of outstanding merit whom the court especially honors are granted specially advanced rank, below the three excellencies but not below the general of chariots and cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang's Han Institutions explains: "Peers of exceptional merit whom the court singles out receive specially advanced rank—below the three excellencies but not beneath the general of chariots and cavalry."

sentences.zh: 赐位朝侯，次五校尉；

translations.literal: those granted the rank of court marquis ranked next after the five colonels;
translations.idiomatic: those given the courtesy rank of “court marquis” followed the five colonels of the guard;

sentences.zh: 赐位侍祠侯，次大夫。

translations.literal: those granted the rank of attendant-sacrifice marquis ranked next after grandees.
translations.idiomatic: and holders of the “attendant-sacrifice marquis” designation stood just after ordinary grandees.

sentences.zh: 其餘以[BD4A]附及公主子孫奉墳墓於京都者，亦隨時見會，位在博士、議郎下。

translations.literal: Hu Guang's Institutions say: "These are called inferior feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang's Institutions calls them "inferior feudal lords."

sentences.zh: 胡廣制度曰：「是爲猥諸侯。」

translations.literal: Hu Guang's Institutions say: "These are called inferior feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang's Institutions calls them "inferior feudal lords."

sentences.zh: 诸王封者受茅土，归以立社稷，礼也。

translations.literal: Those princes who received investiture took the clods of earth with hemp and reeds home to establish the altars of soil and grain; it was proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed kings carried the clod of sacred soil with its tuft of ritual grass back to their capitals to found the altars of soil and grain, as canonical rite prescribed.

sentences.zh: 胡廣曰：「諸王受封，皆受茅土，歸立社稷。

translations.literal: Hu Guang says: "All princes receiving investiture take the clod of earth with ritual grass and return to establish the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang notes: "Enfeoffed princes all receive the sacred clod and return to found the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 本朝爲宮室，自有制度。

translations.literal: The present court builds palaces and has its own institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The present court builds palaces under its own rules.

sentences.zh: 至於列侯歸國者，不受茅土，不立宮室，各隨貧富，裁制黎庶，以守其寵。」

translations.literal: As for full marquises returning to their states, they do not receive the clod of earth, do not build palaces, each according to wealth or poverty regulates the common people to preserve their favor."
translations.idiomatic: Full marquises returning home receive no clod, build no palace, and govern commoners according to their means to keep imperial favor."

sentences.zh: 列土、特進、朝侯賀正月執璧雲。

translations.literal: Full marquises, specially advanced nobles, and court marquises likewise, when congratulating on the first month, held jade discs.
translations.idiomatic: Full marquises, specially advanced peers, and court marquises presented jade tokens at the New Year audience in the same fashion.

sentences.zh: 每国置相一人，其秩各如本县。

translations.literal: Each marquisate placed one chancellor; his salary grade matched the original county.
translations.idiomatic: Every marquisate had a single chancellor whose pay scale matched the underlying county’s rank.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主治民，如令、长，不臣也。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: He governed the people like a magistrate or chief but was not treated as the marquis’s subject minister.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He ruled commoners exactly as a county magistrate would, yet he was not the marquis’s vassal minister—he answered to the throne.

sentences.zh: 但纳租于侯，以户数为限。

translations.literal: They only paid rent to the marquis according to household numbers as the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Tenant households forwarded only the contracted rent to the marquis, capped by registered household counts.

sentences.zh: 其家臣，置家丞、庶子各一人。

translations.literal: For household ministers they placed one household aide and one junior son-of-the-house.
translations.idiomatic: Domestic administration relied on one household aide and one junior steward of the house.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主侍侯，使理家事。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: They attended the marquis and managed household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: These officers served the marquis personally and ran his private establishment.

sentences.zh: 列侯旧有行人、洗马、门大夫，凡五官。

translations.literal: Formerly full marquises had heralds, horse washers, and gate grandees—five offices in all.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system a full marquis kept heralds, outriders who washed the horses at halts, and gate grandees—five household ministries altogether.

sentences.zh: 中兴以来，食邑千户已上置家丞、庶子各一人，不满千户不置家丞，又悉省行人、洗马、门大夫。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, for feoffs of one thousand households or more they placed one household aide and one junior son-of-the-house; below one thousand households they did not place a household aide, and they abolished heralds, horse washers, and gate grandees entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, marquises with at least one thousand feoffed households retained an aide and a junior steward; smaller feoffs lost the household aide, and heralds, washers, and gate grandees were cut altogether.

sentences.zh: 關内侯，如淳曰：「列侯出關就國，侯但爵身，其有家累者與之關内之邑，食其租稅也。」

translations.literal: Marquis-within-the-passes: Ru Chun says: "When full marquises left the passes to go to their states, the marquis kept only the title in person; those with household dependents were given towns within the passes to eat their rent and tax."
translations.idiomatic: Marquis-within-the-passes: Ru Chun explains: "When full marquises left the passes for their states, the title alone went with the holder; dependents were given towns within the passes to draw rent and tax."

sentences.zh: 古今注曰：「建武六年，初令關内侯食邑者俸月二十五斛。」

translations.literal: Notes Ancient and Modern say: "In the sixth year of Jianwu they first ordered that marquises-within-the-passes with food feoffs receive twenty-five hu stipend per month."
translations.idiomatic: Notes Ancient and Modern record: "In Jianwu 6 marquises-within-the-passes with food feoffs were first granted twenty-five hu monthly."

sentences.zh: 关内侯，承秦赐爵十九等，为关内侯，无土，寄食在所县，民租多少，各有户数为限。

translations.literal: Marquis-within-the-passes continued the Qin nineteenth rank as marquis-within-the-passes; they had no territory but lodged grain income in a given county, the people’s rent being limited according to household numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises-within-the-passes inherited the Qin nineteenth-grade title: they held no land but drew a cash-and-grain allowance charged against a host county, with yields prorated to the number of registered households.

sentences.zh: 荀綽晉百官表注曰：「時六國未平，將帥皆家關中，故以爲號。」

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Annotated Jin Table of Officials says: "At that time the six states were not yet pacified; generals and commanders all had homes in Guanzhong, therefore this title was used."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo's Annotated Jin Table of Officials notes: "While the six states were still unconquered, commanders were domiciled in Guanzhong, hence the title."

sentences.zh: 劉劭爵制曰：「春秋傳有庶長鮑。

translations.literal: Liu Shao's Treatise on Ranks says: "The Spring and Autumn Annals mention Chief-of-the-Line Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao's Treatise on Ranks begins: "The Spring and Autumn Annals mention Chief-of-the-Line Bao.

sentences.zh: 商君爲政，備其法品爲十八級，合關内侯、列侯凡二十等，其制因古義。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Shang governed, he completed the legal grades as eighteen ranks; together with marquis-within-the-passes and full marquis there were twenty ranks in all; the system followed ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Shang established eighteen grades; with marquis-within-the-passes and full marquis there were twenty ranks in all, following ancient principle.

sentences.zh: 古者天子寄軍政於六卿，居則以田，警則以戰，所謂入使治之，出使長之，素信者與衆相得也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven entrusted military government to the six ministers: in peace they farmed; in alarm they fought—what is called entering to govern them and going out to lead them; trusted men matched the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Son of Heaven entrusted military affairs to the six ministers: in peace they farmed, in alarm they fought—trusted men leading the multitude.

sentences.zh: 故啓伐有扈，乃召六卿，大夫之在軍爲將者也。

translations.literal: Therefore when Qi attacked Youhu he summoned the six ministers; grandees in the army served as generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi attacked Youhu he summoned the six ministers; grandees in the army served as generals.

sentences.zh: 及周之六卿，亦以居軍，在國也則以比長、閭胥、族師、黨正、州長、卿大夫爲稱，其在軍也則以卒伍、司馬、將軍爲號，所以異在國之名也。

translations.literal: By Zhou's six ministers as well, they dwelt in the army; in the state they were called neighborhood chief, lane clerk, clan instructor, ward rectifier, district chief, and minister-grandee; in the army they were called squad, company, marshal, and general—therefore names in the state differed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's six ministers likewise served in camp; in the state they bore civil titles, in the army military titles—hence the names differed.

sentences.zh: 秦依古制，其在軍賜爵爲等級，其帥人皆更卒也，有功賜爵，則在軍吏之例。

translations.literal: Qin followed the ancient system: in the army ennoblement was granted as grades; those who led men were all corvée soldiers; when merit ennobled them, they fell under the category of army officers.
translations.idiomatic: Qin followed antiquity: army ranks were granted in grades; leaders were corvée soldiers; merit ennoblement made them army officers.

sentences.zh: 自一爵以上至不更四等，皆士也。

translations.literal: From the first rank upward to the fourth rank, Not Replaced, all were shi.
translations.idiomatic: From the first rank through the fourth, Not Replaced, all were common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 大夫以上至五大夫五等，比大夫也。

translations.literal: From grandee upward through the five ranks to Grand Grandee, they were comparable to grandees.
translations.idiomatic: From grandee through the five ranks to Grand Grandee, they were comparable to grandees.

sentences.zh: 九等，依九命之義也。

translations.literal: The nine ranks followed the meaning of the nine commands.
translations.idiomatic: The nine ranks followed the meaning of the nine commands.

sentences.zh: 自左庶長以上至大庶長，九卿之義也。

translations.literal: From Left Chief-of-the-Line upward to Great Chief-of-the-Line followed the meaning of the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: From Left Chief-of-the-Line to Great Chief-of-the-Line followed the meaning of the nine ministers.

sentences.zh: 關内侯者，依古圻内子男之義也。

translations.literal: Marquis-within-the-passes followed the ancient meaning of viscounts and barons within the royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis-within-the-passes followed the ancient meaning of viscounts and barons within the royal domain.

sentences.zh: 秦都山西，以關内爲王畿，故曰關内侯也。

translations.literal: Qin made its capital west of the mountains and took the area within the passes as the royal domain; therefore they were called marquises-within-the-passes.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's capital lay west of the mountains with Guanzhong as the royal domain; hence the title marquis-within-the-passes.

sentences.zh: 列侯者，依古列國諸侯之義也。

translations.literal: Full marquises followed the ancient meaning of feudal lords of ranked states.
translations.idiomatic: Full marquises followed the ancient meaning of feudal lords of ranked states.

sentences.zh: 然則卿大夫士下之品，皆放古，比朝之制而異其名，亦所以殊軍國也。

translations.literal: Thus the grades below ministers, grandees, and shi all imitated antiquity, comparing court institutions while differing in name—this too distinguished army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the lower grades imitated antiquity, matching court institutions under different names to distinguish army and state.

sentences.zh: 古者以車戰，兵車一乘，歩卒七十二人，分翼左右。

translations.literal: In antiquity they fought with chariots; one war chariot had seventy-two foot soldiers, divided to flank left and right.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity one war chariot carried seventy-two foot soldiers flanking left and right.

sentences.zh: 車，大夫在左，御者處中，勇士居右，凡七十五人。

translations.literal: On the chariot the grandee was on the left, the driver in the center, and the brave warrior on the right—seventy-five men in all.
translations.idiomatic: On the chariot the grandee stood left, the driver center, the warrior right—seventy-five men in all.

sentences.zh: 一爵曰公士者，歩卒之有爵爲公士者。

translations.literal: The first rank, called Public Warrior, was a foot soldier who had rank as Public Warrior.
translations.idiomatic: The first rank, Public Warrior, was a ranked foot soldier.

sentences.zh: 二爵曰上造。

translations.literal: The second rank was Upper Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The second rank was Upper Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 造，成也。

translations.literal: Accomplished means completed.
translations.idiomatic: Accomplished means completed.

sentences.zh: 古者成士昇於司徒曰造士，雖依此名，皆歩卒也。

translations.literal: In antiquity accomplished shi who ascended to the minister of education were called Accomplished Shi; though this name was borrowed, all were foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity accomplished shi presented to the minister of education were called Accomplished Shi; though the name was borrowed, all were foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 三爵曰簪褭，御駟馬者。

translations.literal: The third rank was Hairpin Steed, driver of the four-horse team.
translations.idiomatic: The third rank, Hairpin Steed, drove the four-horse team.

sentences.zh: 要褭，古之名馬也。

translations.literal: Yaoniao was an ancient famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoniao was an ancient famous horse.

sentences.zh: 駕駟馬者其形似簪，故曰簪褭也。

translations.literal: The driver of the four-horse team resembled a hairpin in form; therefore it was called Hairpin Steed.
translations.idiomatic: The four-horse driver resembled a hairpin; hence Hairpin Steed.

sentences.zh: 四爵曰不更。

translations.literal: The fourth rank was Not Replaced.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth rank was Not Replaced.

sentences.zh: 不更者，爲車右，不復與凡更卒同也。

translations.literal: Not Replaced meant serving as chariot right; one no longer shared duties with ordinary corvée soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Not Replaced meant chariot right, no longer sharing duties with ordinary corvée soldiers.

sentences.zh: 五爵曰大夫。

translations.literal: The fifth rank was grandee.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth rank was grandee.

sentences.zh: 大夫者，在車左者也。

translations.literal: Grandee meant the one on the left of the chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee meant the one on the left of the chariot.

sentences.zh: 六爵爲官大夫，七爵爲公大夫，八爵爲公乘，九爵爲五大夫，皆軍吏也。

translations.literal: The sixth rank was Officer Grandee, the seventh Public Grandee, the eighth Public Chariot, the ninth Grand Grandee—all army officers.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth through ninth ranks—Officer Grandee, Public Grandee, Public Chariot, and Grand Grandee—were all army officers.

sentences.zh: 吏民爵不得過公乘者，得貰與子若同産。

translations.literal: Commoners whose rank could not exceed Public Chariot might transfer it to a son or same-birth kin.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners capped at Public Chariot could transfer rank to a son or same-birth kin.

sentences.zh: 然則公乘者，軍吏之爵髙者也。

translations.literal: Thus Public Chariot was a high rank among army officers.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Public Chariot was a high rank among army officers.

sentences.zh: 雖非臨戰，得公卒車，故曰公乘也。

translations.literal: Though not in battle, one could obtain a public soldier's chariot; therefore it was called Public Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Though not in battle one could obtain a public soldier's chariot; hence Public Chariot.

sentences.zh: 十爵爲左庶長，十一爵爲右庶長，十二爵爲左更，十三爵爲中更，十四爵爲右更，十五爵爲少上造，十六爵爲大上造，十七爵爲駟車庶長，十八爵爲大庶長，十九爵爲關内侯，二十爵爲列侯。

translations.literal: The tenth rank was Left Chief-of-the-Line, the eleventh Right Chief-of-the-Line, the twelfth Left Renewer, the thirteenth Central Renewer, the fourteenth Right Renewer, the fifteenth Lesser Upper Accomplished, the sixteenth Greater Upper Accomplished, the seventeenth Four-Chariot Chief-of-the-Line, the eighteenth Great Chief-of-the-Line, the nineteenth marquis-within-the-passes, the twentieth full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks ten through twenty ran from Left Chief-of-the-Line through Right Renewer, Lesser and Greater Upper Accomplished, Four-Chariot and Great Chief-of-the-Line, marquis-within-the-passes, and full marquis.

sentences.zh: 自左庶長已上至大庶長，皆卿大夫，皆軍將也。

translations.literal: From Left Chief-of-the-Line upward to Great Chief-of-the-Line, all were ministers and grandees, all army generals.
translations.idiomatic: From Left Chief-of-the-Line to Great Chief-of-the-Line all were ministers and grandees, all army generals.

sentences.zh: 所將皆庶人、更卒也，故以庶更爲名。

translations.literal: Those they led were all commoners and corvée soldiers; therefore the names used commoner and renewer.
translations.idiomatic: Those they led were commoners and corvée soldiers; hence the names commoner and renewer.

sentences.zh: 大庶長卽大將軍也，左右庶長卽左右偏裨將軍也。」

translations.literal: Great Chief-of-the-Line was the grand general; Left and Right Chiefs-of-the-Line were left and right assistant generals."
translations.idiomatic: Great Chief-of-the-Line was the grand general; Left and Right Chiefs-of-the-Line were left and right assistant generals."

sentences.zh: 古今注曰：「成帝鴻嘉三年，令吏民得買爵，級千錢。」

translations.literal: Notes Ancient and Modern say: "In the third year of Hongjia of Emperor Cheng, commoners and officials were allowed to buy ranks at one thousand cash per grade."
translations.idiomatic: Notes Ancient and Modern record: "In Hongjia 3 of Emperor Cheng, officials and commoners were allowed to buy ranks at one thousand cash per grade."

sentences.zh: 四夷国王，率众王，归义侯，邑君，邑长，皆有丞，比郡、县。

translations.literal: Kings of the four quarters, chieftains-at-heads-of-crowds, marquises who had submitted in righteousness, town lords, and town chiefs all had assistants, comparable to commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Tributary kings, tribal “chiefs who lead hosts,” marquises of submission, town lords, and town chiefs each received deputy officers modeled on commandery and county assistants.

sentences.zh: 百官受奉例：大将军、三公奉，月三百五十斛。

translations.literal: Examples of official stipends: the grand general and the three excellencies received three hundred fifty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Stipends were reckoned in grain: the grand general and the three excellencies drew three hundred fifty hu a month.

sentences.zh: 中二千石奉，月百八十斛。

translations.literal: For fully two thousand piculs the stipend was one hundred eighty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at the “full two thousand picul” grade received one hundred eighty hu monthly.

sentences.zh: 二千石奉，月百二十斛。

translations.literal: For two thousand piculs the stipend was one hundred twenty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: A straight two-thousand-picul salary meant one hundred twenty hu each month.

sentences.zh: 比二千石奉，月百斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to two thousand piculs the stipend was one hundred hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: The “comparable to two thousand piculs” band paid one hundred hu.

sentences.zh: 千石奉，月八十斛。

translations.literal: For one thousand piculs the stipend was eighty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: One-thousand-picul posts drew eighty hu.

sentences.zh: 六百石奉，月七十斛。

translations.literal: For six hundred piculs the stipend was seventy hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Six-hundred-picul officials took seventy hu.

sentences.zh: 比六百石奉，月五十斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to six hundred piculs the stipend was fifty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: The “comparable to six hundred” grade received fifty hu.

sentences.zh: 四百石奉，月四十五斛。

translations.literal: For four hundred piculs the stipend was forty-five hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Four-hundred-picul salaries came to forty-five hu.

sentences.zh: 比四百石奉，月四十斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to four hundred piculs the stipend was forty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Comparable to four hundred meant forty hu.

sentences.zh: 三百石奉，月四十斛。

translations.literal: For three hundred piculs the stipend was forty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Three-hundred-picul posts oddly matched forty hu as well.

sentences.zh: 比三百石奉，月三十七斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to three hundred piculs the stipend was thirty-seven hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Comparable to three hundred paid thirty-seven hu.

sentences.zh: 二百石奉，月三十斛。

translations.literal: For two hundred piculs the stipend was thirty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Two-hundred-picul clerks drew thirty hu.

sentences.zh: 比二百石奉，月二十七斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to two hundred piculs the stipend was twenty-seven hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Comparable to two hundred meant twenty-seven hu.

sentences.zh: 一百石奉，月十六斛。

translations.literal: For one hundred piculs the stipend was sixteen hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: One-hundred-picul minor officials received sixteen hu.

sentences.zh: 斗食奉，月十一斛。

translations.literal: For dou-food clerks the stipend was eleven hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Dou-food subclerks—paid by the peck—took eleven hu monthly.

sentences.zh: 佐史奉，月八斛。

translations.literal: For assistant clerks the stipend was eight hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant clerks at the bottom of the scale drew eight hu.

sentences.zh: 凡诸受奉，皆半钱半谷。

translations.literal: In general all who received stipends received half in cash and half in grain.
translations.idiomatic: Every grade on the schedule was normally split half in coin and half in unhusked grain.

sentences.zh: 荀綽《晉百官表注》曰：「漢延平中，中二千石奉錢九千，米七十二斛。

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Annotated Table of Jin Offices says: "In the Han period of Yanping, those at the middle two-thousand-picul grade received nine thousand in cash and seventy-two hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo's Annotated Table of Jin Offices records: "Under the Han in Yanping, middle two-thousand-picul officials drew nine thousand cash and seventy-two hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 眞二千石月錢六千五百，米三十六斛。

translations.literal: True two-thousand-picul officials received six thousand five hundred cash per month and thirty-six hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: True two-thousand-picul officers took six thousand five hundred cash monthly and thirty-six hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 比二千石月錢五千，米三十四斛。

translations.literal: Comparable two-thousand-picul officials received five thousand cash per month and thirty-four hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Comparable two-thousand-picul officers drew five thousand cash monthly and thirty-four hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 一千石月錢四千，米三十斛。

translations.literal: One-thousand-picul officials received four thousand cash per month and thirty hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: One-thousand-picul officers took four thousand cash monthly and thirty hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 六百石月錢三千五百，米二十一斛。

translations.literal: Six-hundred-picul officials received three thousand five hundred cash per month and twenty-one hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Six-hundred-picul officers drew three thousand five hundred cash monthly and twenty-one hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 四百石月錢二千五百，米十五斛。

translations.literal: Four-hundred-picul officials received two thousand five hundred cash per month and fifteen hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Four-hundred-picul officers took two thousand five hundred cash monthly and fifteen hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 三百石月錢二千，米十二斛。

translations.literal: Three-hundred-picul officials received two thousand cash per month and twelve hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Three-hundred-picul officers drew two thousand cash monthly and twelve hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 二百石月錢一千，米九斛。

translations.literal: Two-hundred-picul officials received one thousand cash per month and nine hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Two-hundred-picul officers took one thousand cash monthly and nine hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 百石月錢八百，米四斛八斗。」

translations.literal: One-hundred-picul officials received eight hundred cash per month and four hu eight dou of grain."
translations.idiomatic: One-hundred-picul officers drew eight hundred cash monthly and four hu eight dou of grain."

sentences.zh: 獻帝起居注曰：「帝在長安，詔書以三輔地不滿千里，而軍師用度非一，公卿已下不得奏除。

translations.literal: The Daily Records of Emperor Xian say: "When the emperor was in Chang'an, an edict declared that because the three adjuncts covered less than a thousand li and military expenses were manifold, officials from the excellencies down could not memorialize appointments and removals.
translations.idiomatic: The Daily Records of Emperor Xian note: "At Chang'an the emperor ruled that because the three adjuncts spanned less than a thousand li yet military costs were heavy, no official below the excellencies might propose appointments or dismissals.

translations.literal: As for public fields, according to salary grade
translations.idiomatic: For public fields, graded by salary rank, revenue was

translations.idiomatic: (Yu)

sentences.zh: 〔與〕令各自收其租稅。」

translations.literal: [was allotted] and magistrates each collected their own rent and tax."
translations.idiomatic: [allotted] and each magistrate collected the rents and taxes himself."

sentences.zh: 赞曰：帝道渊默，冢帅修德。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The imperial way is deep and silent; the high ministers at the ancestral shrine cultivate virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The summation reads: The royal path runs silent and deep; the chief ministers who stand at the high altar polish their virtue.

sentences.zh: 寡以御众，分职乃克。

translations.literal: With few principles he governed the many; only when offices were divided could it succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler guides the multitude through restraint; order comes only when every office keeps its brief.

sentences.zh: 不置不监，无骄无忒。

translations.literal: What is not set up is not supervised; there is neither arrogance nor transgression.
translations.idiomatic: Leave unneeded posts unfilled and they need no overseers—then there is neither swagger among officials nor dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 程是师徒，宁民康国。

translations.literal: Take these masters and disciples as your model, and the people are quieted and the state is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hold this cadre of teachers and followers to the standard, and the common people find rest while the realm flourishes in peace.
